Coming from napi-rs
docs.markdown:
# Coming from napi-rs

napi-go follows the design of napi-rs: annotated declarations, conversions from the types of the
language, TypeScript declarations, one npm package per platform. The table maps the napi-rs
features to napi-go.

## Code

| napi-rs | napi-go |
|---|---|
| `#[napi] fn add(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64` | `//napi:export` on `func Add(a, b float64) float64` |
| `#[napi(js_name = "x")]` | `//napi:export x` |
| `#[napi(object)] struct` | any struct converts; `//napi:object` declares it in `index.d.ts` even when unused |
| `#[napi] struct` + `#[napi] impl` (class) | `//napi:class` on the type; exported methods of `*T` |
| `#[napi(constructor)]`, `#[napi(factory)]` | `//napi:constructor` (`func(…) (*T, error)`); `//napi:export Class.name` for a static factory |
| `#[napi(getter)]`, `#[napi(setter)]` | `//napi:getter`, `//napi:setter` |
| `#[napi(skip)]` | `//napi:skip` |
| `#[napi] const` | `//napi:export` on a constant |
| `#[napi(ts_type = "…")]`, `ts_return_type` | `//napi:type`, `//napi:returns` |
| `Result<T>`, `Error::new(Status::InvalidArg, msg)` | `(T, error)`; `napi.TypeError(code, msg)`, `napi.RangeError` |
| a panic | a panic becomes an Error with code `GO_PANIC` |
| `async fn` (tokio) | a first parameter `context.Context`: the function runs in a goroutine |
| `AsyncTask` with `Task` | `Env.Async(work)`: `work` runs in a goroutine and returns a `Resolver` run on the JS thread |
| `AbortSignal` of an `AsyncTask` | no counterpart: the `context.Context` is canceled only when the env is destroyed |
| `ThreadsafeFunction<T>` | `napi.NewThreadsafeFunction[T]` |
| `ThreadsafeFunction::call_async` | `napi.NewJSFunc[A, R]`, `Call(ctx, a)` |
| `Function<A, R>`, `JsFunction` | `napi.Function` |
| `Either<A, B>` | `napi.Either[A, B]` |
| `Buffer`, `&[u8]`, `Uint8Array` | `[]byte`: a view as a parameter, a copy as a result (`Env.NewBuffer` for no copy) |
| `BigInt`, `i64` | `*big.Int`, `int64` (integers are range-checked) |
| `Option<T>` | `*T` |
| `HashMap<String, T>` | `map[string]T` |
| `ObjectFinalize` | `func (*T) Finalize(env napi.Env)` |
| `Reference<T>` to a class instance | the `*T` itself: in an env the same `*T` is always the same JS object |
| `Env` | `napi.Env` (a parameter of type `napi.Env` is injected) |
| `JsObject`, `JsUnknown` | `napi.Object`, `napi.Value` |
| `#[module_exports]` | `napi.Init` (Layer 1) |

## Tooling

| `@napi-rs/cli` | `napi-go` |
|---|---|
| `napi new` | `napi-go new` |
| `napi build --release --target …` | `napi-go build -release -target …` (zig for other platforms) |
| type generation of `napi build` | `napi-go gen` (run by `build`) |
| `napi create-npm-dirs`, `napi artifacts` | `napi-go artifacts` |
| `napi prepublish` | `napi-go prepublish -publish` |
| `"napi"` in `package.json` | `"napiGo"` |
| targets `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, … | targets `linux-x64-gnu`, … (the platform package suffixes, as in napi-rs) |

The CLI is a Go program run with `go tool napi-go`, at the version of the library in `go.mod`;
it does not need npm.

## Differences

- **Call overhead.** A call into Go crosses from C into the Go runtime (about 100 ns on Linux,
  about 1 µs on Windows), where napi-rs calls Rust directly. Conversions of numbers and short
  strings happen in C in the same crossing. Bulk Promises are cheaper than in napi-rs. See the
  [benchmarks](../bench/README.md).
- **Binary size.** The Go runtime is part of every addon: a small addon is about 2.5 MB stripped,
  against well under 1 MB for napi-rs.
- **Platforms.** No musl (Alpine): Go cannot build shared libraries that load with musl. On macOS
  x64 only one Go addon can be loaded per process. No WebAssembly target. See
  [platforms](platforms.md).
- **Two garbage collectors.** Go values referenced from JS live until V8 collects the JS object;
  a `[]byte` parameter must not be kept after the call.
- **Concurrency.** Goroutines replace the tokio runtime and the libuv thread pool; there is no
  runtime to configure.

docs.title: Platforms and limitations
docs.markdown:
# Platforms and limitations

## Supported

| Target | Built from | Tested in CI |
|---|---|---|
| `linux-x64-gnu` | any host (zig: glibc 2.17 or later) | Node 22, 24, 26, current; Go 1.24 and stable |
| `linux-arm64-gnu` | any host (zig: glibc 2.17 or later) | Node 22, 24, 26; Go 1.24 and stable |
| `darwin-arm64` | macOS, or any host with zig | Node 22, 24, 26; Go 1.24 and stable |
| `darwin-x64` | macOS, or any host with zig | Node 22, 24, 26; Go 1.24 and stable |
| `win32-x64-gnu` | Windows (MinGW gcc or zig), or any host with zig | Node 22, 24, 26; Go 1.24 and stable |
| `win32-arm64-gnu` | any host with zig | Node 24: binaries built with zig, loaded and tested |

- **Go** 1.24 or later (the `tool` directive of `go.mod` used by the template needs 1.24).
- **Node.js** 22 or later is tested. Addons declare Node-API 8 by default (Node.js 12.22 and later
  provide it); the build tags `napi_go_v9` and `napi_go_v10` declare 9 and 10 for their functions
  and behaviors.
- **Worker threads**: supported; each worker loads the addon in its own env.
- **Electron**: not tested. Where external buffers are not allowed (the V8 sandbox), napi-go copies
  instead.

## Known limitations

- **musl (Alpine Linux) is not supported.** No Go release builds a shared library that loads with
  musl: `dlopen` rejects the initial-exec TLS of the Go runtime (golang/go#71953; the Go change
  CL 696635 fixes it and is tracked in CI). The loader in `index.js` explains it on musl.
- **macOS x64: one Go addon per process.** On darwin/amd64 every Go runtime uses the same TLS slot
  for the current goroutine (golang/go#23617). A second napi-go addon (or any other Go c-shared
  library) is rejected with `ERR_NAPI_GO_FOREIGN_RUNTIME` instead of corrupting memory. macOS arm64,
  Linux and Windows load any number of Go addons.
- **Windows: a call costs about 1 µs**, against about 100 ns on Linux: the Go runtime lacks an
  optimization for threads created outside Go on Windows (`x_cgo_bindm`).
- **Binary size**: the Go runtime is in every addon, about 2.5 MB for a small one (stripped).
- **Not wrapped yet**: async hooks (`napi_async_init`, `napi_make_callback`), the libuv thread pool
  (`napi_async_work`) and SharedArrayBuffer are only in `sys`; asynchronous class methods are not
  supported by Layer 2 (call `Env.Async` in a method). See the
  [current limitations](../napi/README.md#current-limitations).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `cannot load the native addon … for linux-x64-musl` | musl is not supported: use a glibc-based image (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, `node:*-slim`) |
| `cannot load the native addon … package not installed` | the platform package was not installed: `npm install` with optional dependencies enabled (not `--omit=optional`), on the same platform as the one that runs the code |
| `GLIBC_2.xx not found` | the binary was built against a newer glibc: build with zig (`napi-go build -release`, the default when zig is installed) |
| `ERR_NAPI_GO_FOREIGN_RUNTIME` | macOS x64: a second Go addon in the process (see above) |
| `ERR_NAPI_GO_MISSING_FUNCTIONS` | the Node.js version lacks Node-API functions of the declared version: drop the `napi_go_v9`/`napi_go_v10` tag or update Node.js |
| `cross-compiling for … needs zig` | install [zig](https://ziglang.org/download/) or build on that platform |
| `cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found` (Windows) | install MinGW gcc, or use `napi-go build -zig always` with zig |
| a TypeError `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` from an addon function | a JS argument of the wrong type: the message names the argument and the path inside it |
| a `GO_PANIC` error | a panic in the Go function; its message is the panic value |

To see what `index.js` tried, read the error: it lists every candidate (local file, platform
package) with the reason it failed. `NAPI_GO_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/addon.node` loads a
specific binary.

docs.title: Releasing napi-go
docs.markdown:
# Releasing napi-go

napi-go is a Go module: a release is a git tag `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Users get it with
`go get github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go@<tag>` and run the CLI of the same version with
`go tool napi-go` (or `go run github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go/cmd/napi-go@<tag>`).

## Checklist

1. **`main` is green**: the workflows `sys`, `cli` and `bench` on the commit to release.
2. **CHANGELOG.md**: the section of the version lists the changes and has the date of the release,
   `## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-20` (the release workflow refuses a section without a date).
3. **Commit** the changelog to `main`, then **tag** that commit and push the tag:

   ```sh
   git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "napi-go 0.1.0"
   git push origin v0.1.0
   ```

4. **The release workflow** ([`release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml)) then:
   - checks the tag against CHANGELOG.md and extracts the release notes;
   - builds the CLI for Linux, macOS and Windows (x64 and arm64), with `SHA256SUMS`, and checks
     that it reports the tag as its version;
   - on Linux, macOS and Windows, creates a project with
     `go run github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go/cmd/napi-go@<tag> new`, fetching the tag from
     GitHub as a user would, then builds and tests it;
   - creates the GitHub release with the notes and the binaries (a pre-release for tags such as
     `v0.2.0-rc.1`).
5. **Make the version known to the Go proxy and pkg.go.dev**:

   ```sh
   GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go@v0.1.0
   ```

   then open `https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go@v0.1.0` (the page appears within
   minutes, or request it there).
6. **Start the next section** of CHANGELOG.md: `## [Unreleased]`.

If the release workflow fails, fix the cause on `main` and release a new patch version: a tag
published to the Go proxy cannot be changed. Until the proxy has fetched it, a wrong tag can still
be deleted (`git push origin :refs/tags/v0.1.0`) and created again.

## Versions

- Before 1.0.0 a minor version may change the API; CHANGELOG.md lists the changes.
- napi-go supports the two latest Go releases (with cgo) and the Node.js versions tested in CI
  (currently 22, 24 and 26). Addons declare Node-API 8 unless built with `napi_go_v9` or
  `napi_go_v10`.
- The CLI and the library share the module version: projects pin both with `go.mod`.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.markdown:
# Benchmarks

The same addon written three ways, each the idiomatic way of its framework:

| Implementation | Source | How it is written |
|---|---|---|
| napi-go | [`napigo/main.go`](napigo/main.go) | `//napi:export` annotations, registrations generated by `napi-go gen` (Layer 2) |
| napi-rs | [`napi-rs/src/lib.rs`](napi-rs/src/lib.rs) | `#[napi]`, `async fn` on the tokio runtime of napi-rs |
| node-addon-api | [`node-addon-api/addon.cc`](node-addon-api/addon.cc) | C++ with the same argument checks, `Napi::AsyncWorker` (libuv thread pool) |

and plain JavaScript as a reference for the cost of the JS side of each case.

| Case | What it measures |
|---|---|
| `noop()` | the cost of a call |
| `add(a, b)` | two numbers in, one out |
| `echo(s)` | a string converted to the native language and back (16 B, 1 KiB, 64 KiB, ASCII) |
| `bufferLength(b)` | a 1 MiB Buffer read in place (no copy) |
| `makeBuffer(n)` | a new zero-filled 1 MiB Buffer returned to JS |
| `await resolveAsync(n)`, one at a time | latency of a Promise resolved by a background thread |
| `resolveAsync(n)` × 1000 with `Promise.all` | throughput of Promises resolved by background threads |

## Running

Requirements: Go with cgo, Node.js 22 or later; for napi-rs, Rust (cargo); for node-addon-api, a
C++ compiler and the Node.js headers (on Linux and macOS: the official Node.js builds include
them). An implementation that cannot be built is skipped.

```sh
cd bench && npm ci && cd ..
node bench/build.mjs                       # bench/build/{napigo,napi-rs,node-addon-api}.node
node bench/run.mjs                         # about two minutes
node bench/run.mjs --quick --filter echo   # fewer samples, only the matching cases
node bench/run.mjs --json results.json
```

`run.mjs` first checks that every implementation returns the same results, and that the native
ones throw for an argument of the wrong type. It then calibrates each case so that a sample lasts
about 100 ms, interleaves the samples of the implementations (one round runs each once, so a change
of machine load affects all of them alike), discards three warm-up rounds and reports the median
of 15 samples. The CI workflow [`bench.yml`](../.github/workflows/bench.yml) runs it on Linux and
macOS and writes the table to the summary of the run.

## Results

Linux x64 (2 vCPU, Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz), Node.js 22.23, Go 1.24.7, Rust 1.97, g++ 13.3,
2026-11-12. Times are medians per operation; lower is better.

| Case | napi-go | napi-rs | node-addon-api | plain JS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| noop() | 136 ns | 29 ns | 24 ns | 4.0 ns |
| add(a, b) | 170 ns | 117 ns | 44 ns | 8.4 ns |
| echo(string of 16 B) | 237 ns | 213 ns | 121 ns | 7.4 ns |
| echo(string of 1 KiB) | 1.61 µs | 644 ns | 503 ns | 7.6 ns |
| echo(string of 64 KiB) | 44.1 µs | 22.7 µs | 22.6 µs | 7.2 ns |
| bufferLength(Buffer of 1 MiB) | 353 ns | 128 ns | 60 ns | 7.7 ns |
| makeBuffer(1 MiB) | 259 µs | 130 µs | 112 µs | 54.4 µs |
| await resolveAsync(n), one at a time | 46.6 µs | 30.2 µs | 31.1 µs | 52 ns |
| resolveAsync(n) × 1000 with Promise.all | 1.90 µs | 10.8 µs | 6.11 µs | 109 ns |

Between two runs the results differ by a few percent, except the Promise awaited one at a time,
whose napi-go time ranged from 45 to 90 µs (it is the latency of waking a goroutine and then the
JS thread, sensitive to scheduling on two CPUs).

## Reading the results

- **The floor of a call is the cgo callback, about 100 ns.** Node.js calls the addon on its own
  thread, which is not a Go thread: entering Go from C costs about 100 ns (`runtime.cgocallback`),
  against a direct function call for Rust and C++. Every napi-go function pays it once; the
  conversions of numbers, booleans and short strings then run in C in the same crossing (the typed
  trampoline, `sys/typed.c`), which is why `add` costs only 34 ns more than `noop`.
- **Short strings are close to napi-rs; long ones are about twice as slow.** Up to about 500 bytes
  a string is read in C in the same crossing. A longer one falls back to Go
  (`Value.GoString`): a first read into a 256-byte buffer, a query of the length and a second read,
  each one a cgo crossing in which V8 scans the whole string. napi-rs and node-addon-api query the
  length and read once.
- **`[]byte` parameters are not handled by the typed trampoline**: reading a Buffer takes two more
  crossings from Go (`napi_is_typedarray`, `napi_get_typedarray_info`), about 220 ns. The data is
  not copied: the cost does not depend on the size.
- **A returned `[]byte` is copied.** `makeBuffer` allocates and clears 1 MiB on the Go heap, then
  Node-API copies it into a new Buffer (`napi_create_buffer_copy`); with allocations of this size
  the Go garbage collector runs about every third call (332 cycles in 1,000 calls with
  `GODEBUG=gctrace=1`). napi-rs hands its `Vec` to V8 without copying
  (external buffer). In napi-go, `Env.NewBuffer` (Layer 1) creates the Buffer in V8 memory and
  returns a `[]byte` view to fill, without the copy.
- **Promises in bulk are 3–6 times faster than napi-rs and node-addon-api.** napi-go settles
  Promises through one threadsafe function per env with a Go queue, and wakes the JS thread only
  when the queue becomes non-empty: a thousand goroutines finishing together cost one wake-up.
  napi-rs and node-addon-api pay one per Promise. The latency of a single Promise is higher
  (a goroutine wakes up, then the JS thread).

Candidate optimizations, measured here: reading a long string with one length query and one read
(and without the 256-byte attempt when the typed trampoline has already found the string too long),
`[]byte` parameters in the typed trampoline, and returned `[]byte` written into a Buffer allocated
by V8 instead of copied.

docs.title: napi-go (CLI)
docs.markdown:
# napi-go (CLI)

Creates, builds and packages Node.js addons written in Go: the equivalent of the `napi` CLI of
napi-rs.

```sh
go run github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go/cmd/napi-go@latest new my-addon
cd my-addon
npm run build:debug        # go tool napi-go build
npm test
```

A project created by `new` requires napi-go in `go.mod` both as a library and as a
[tool](https://go.dev/doc/modules/managing-dependencies#tools), so the CLI runs at the version of
the library with `go tool napi-go <command>`.

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `new <dir>` | create a project: `go.mod`, an annotated `main.go`, `package.json`, a `node:test` test, `.gitignore`, `README.md` and a GitHub Actions workflow |
| `gen` | generate `zz_napi.go`, `index.js` and `index.d.ts` from the `//napi:` annotations ([`internal/codegen`](../../internal/codegen/README.md)) |
| `build` | `go build -buildmode=c-shared` for this machine or other targets, after `gen` |
| `artifacts` | copy built binaries into the npm platform packages `npm/<target>/` |
| `prepublish` | sync the platform packages and `optionalDependencies` with the version; `-publish` publishes the platform packages |
| `version` | print the version |

Every command takes `-C <dir>` (the project, default `.`) and describes its flags with `-h`.

## Configuration

`package.json` holds the configuration under `napiGo`; every field is optional.

```json
{
  "name": "@acme/fast-thing",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "main": "index.js",
  "types": "index.d.ts",
  "napiGo": {
    "binaryName": "fast-thing",
    "goPackage": ".",
    "targets": ["linux-x64-gnu", "linux-arm64-gnu", "darwin-x64", "darwin-arm64", "win32-x64-gnu"],
    "tags": "",
    "codegen": true,
    "js": "index.js",
    "dts": "index.d.ts",
    "npmDir": "npm"
  }
}
```

| Field | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `binaryName` | the package name without scope | binaries are `<binaryName>.<target>.node` |
| `goPackage` | `.` | directory of the Go main package |
| `targets` | the five above | built by `build -target all` and published |
| `tags` | none | Go build tags |
| `codegen` | `true` | `build` runs `gen` first |
| `js`, `dts` | `index.js`, `index.d.ts` | generated entry point and declarations |
| `npmDir` | `npm` | directory of the platform packages |

Without `package.json`, `gen` and `build` work on the Go package in the directory, named after it.

## Targets

Targets are named like the platform packages of napi-rs: `<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]`, from
`process.platform` and `process.arch`.

| Target | GOOS/GOARCH | zig target | Runner of the CI template |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linux-x64-gnu` | linux/amd64 | `x86_64-linux-gnu.2.17` | `ubuntu-latest` |
| `linux-arm64-gnu` | linux/arm64 | `aarch64-linux-gnu.2.17` | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` |
| `darwin-x64` | darwin/amd64 | `x86_64-macos.11.0` | `macos-15-intel` |
| `darwin-arm64` | darwin/arm64 | `aarch64-macos.11.0` | `macos-latest` |
| `win32-x64-gnu` | windows/amd64 | `x86_64-windows-gnu` | `windows-latest` |
| `win32-arm64-gnu` | windows/arm64 | `aarch64-windows-gnu` | `windows-11-arm` |

Windows targets end in `-gnu` because Go links with MinGW. musl (Alpine) is rejected: no Go
release builds a shared library that loads with musl (golang/go#71953). On macOS x64 only one
napi-go addon can be loaded per process (a limit of the Go runtime, see `sys/README.md`).

## Building and cross-compiling

```sh
go tool napi-go build                                   # debug build for this machine
go tool napi-go build -release                          # -ldflags="-s -w"
go tool napi-go build -release -target all              # every target of package.json
go tool napi-go build -target linux-arm64-gnu,win32-x64-gnu -o dist
go tool napi-go build -- -a                             # after --: further go build flags
```

Cross builds use [zig](https://ziglang.org/download/) as C compiler (`zig cc -target …`), from any
host to any target. `-zig` chooses when:

- `auto` (default): cross builds, and release builds for Linux, so that the binary needs glibc 2.17
  rather than the glibc of the build machine (without zig a warning says so);
- `always`: every build (for instance Windows without MinGW);
- `never`: the system C compiler (`$CC`); cross builds then need `-cc`.

`-cc <command>` sets the C compiler of every target instead. macOS builds the other architecture
with the system clang. For macOS targets built elsewhere, the CLI provides zig with stubs of
`libresolv` and of the CoreFoundation framework, which Go links and zig does not ship (the real
libraries are loaded at run time).

After each build the format of the binary is checked against the target (ELF, Mach-O or PE,
architecture, shared library), so a wrong `$CC` fails the build instead of the `require()`.

## The entry point

`gen` writes `index.js`, which loads the binary of the running platform, trying in order:

1. `NAPI_GO_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`, if set (its errors are not caught);
2. `<binaryName>.<target>.node` and `<binaryName>.node` next to `index.js` (local builds);
3. the package `<name>-<target>` (published builds).

If none loads, the error lists each candidate with the reason (`not found`, `package not
installed`, or the error of `dlopen`), with the errors as `cause`. On musl it says that musl is not
supported. `index.js` ends with the export names in the form `0 && (module.exports = { … })`,
which Node reads (and never runs) to let ES modules import them by name.

## Publishing

As with napi-rs, every target has an npm package `<name>-<target>` holding its `.node` file, with
`os`, `cpu` and, on Linux, `libc`; the main package lists them in `optionalDependencies` and npm
installs only the one matching the machine.

```sh
go tool napi-go artifacts -d artifacts   # find <binaryName>.<target>.node files (recursively) and copy them to npm/<target>/
go tool napi-go prepublish -publish      # versions, optionalDependencies, npm publish of each platform package
npm publish                              # the main package
```

`artifacts` creates or updates `npm/<target>/package.json` (fields it does not manage are kept)
and rejects a binary whose format does not match its target. `prepublish` fails if a binary is
missing; with `-publish` it skips the packages already on the registry at this version, so a
failed release can be rerun. `-tag` and `-dry-run` are passed to `npm publish`; scoped packages
are published with `--access public` unless `package.json` has `publishConfig`.

The workflow created by `new` (`.github/workflows/CI.yml`) builds and tests each target on a
runner of that platform, and for a tag `v<version>` checks that the tag matches `package.json`,
then runs the three commands above (secret `NPM_TOKEN`, with npm provenance).

docs.title: napi-go gen
docs.markdown:
# napi-go gen

The code generator of the [`napi-go`](../../cmd/napi-go/README.md) CLI. Generates the Layer 2 registrations and the TypeScript declarations of a napi-go addon from
annotations in its Go source: the equivalent of `#[napi]` and of the type generation of napi-rs.

```go
package main

//go:generate go tool napi-go gen

import "context"

// User is a registered user.
type User struct {
	Name  string
	Email *string
}

// Greet returns a greeting for u.
//
//napi:export
func Greet(u User) string { return "hello " + u.Name }

// FindUser loads a user in a goroutine.
//
//napi:export
func FindUser(ctx context.Context, name string) (*User, error) { return &User{Name: name}, nil }

func main() {}
```

`napi-go gen` (run by `napi-go build`, or by `go generate`) writes three files:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `zz_napi.go` | an `init` function calling `napi.Export` for every annotated declaration, with the wrapper that fits each signature (`Func1`, `Async1`, `MethodE2`, …) |
| `index.d.ts` | TypeScript declarations; the Go doc comments become JSDoc |
| `index.js` | CommonJS entry point loading the binary of the platform (see the [CLI](../../cmd/napi-go/README.md#the-entry-point)) |

```ts
/** User is a registered user. */
export interface User {
  name: string
  email?: string | null
}

/** Greet returns a greeting for u. */
export declare function greet(u: User): string

/** FindUser loads a user in a goroutine. */
export declare function findUser(name: string): Promise<User | null>
```

Problems are reported when generating, with file and line, instead of when the addon is loaded:

```
main.go:14: func Watch: parameter 1: type chan int has no JS conversion
```

## Annotations

Annotations are written like Go directives, with no space after `//`, in the doc comment of the
declaration. An unknown or misplaced annotation is an error.

| Annotation | On | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `//napi:export [name]` | function | exported function; `name` defaults to the Go name in lowerCamelCase. A first parameter of type `context.Context` makes it asynchronous (it runs in a goroutine and returns a Promise) |
| `//napi:export Class.name` | function, constant | static method or static constant of a class |
| `//napi:export [name]` | constant, variable | exported constant (the value when the addon is loaded) |
| `//napi:class [Name]` | type | JS class whose instances wrap a `*T`. Every exported method of `*T` becomes a method, except `Finalize`, `FromJS`, `ToJS` and those marked `//napi:skip` |
| `//napi:constructor` | function returning `(*T, error)` | constructor of the class of `T`. Without one the class cannot be constructed from JS |
| `//napi:export name` | method | renames the method |
| `//napi:getter [name]` | method `func (*T) X() V` | property getter (`V, error` allowed) |
| `//napi:setter [name]` | method `func (*T) SetX(v V)` | setter of the property with the same name; the default name drops the `Set` prefix |
| `//napi:skip` | method | not exported |
| `//napi:object [Name]` | struct type | emits its interface even if no export uses it, optionally renamed. Structs used by an export are emitted without it |
| `//napi:type <TypeScript type>` | type | TypeScript type of a type that converts itself (`FromJS`/`ToJS`), `any` otherwise |
| `//napi:returns <TypeScript type>` | function, method | overrides the declared return type (e.g. `this`, or `Promise<string[]>` for a function returning a `napi.Promise`) |

Functions take up to 8 parameters and return nothing, a value, an error, or a value and an error;
asynchronous functions return `(R, error)` or `error`. Parameters of type `napi.Env` and
`napi.CallContext` are filled by napi and do not appear in the declarations (`CallContext` adds
`...args: any[]`). Variadic and generic functions, asynchronous methods and classes used by value
(`T` instead of `*T`) are rejected with an explanation.

## TypeScript mapping

| Go | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `bool`, `string` | `boolean`, `string` |
| numeric types | `number`; `int64` and `uint64` parameters: `number \| bigint` |
| `[]byte` | parameter: `Uint8Array \| ArrayBuffer \| DataView`; result: `Buffer`; field: `Uint8Array` |
| `*big.Int`, `time.Time` | `bigint`, `Date` |
| `[]T`, `[N]T` | `T[]`; a tuple for N ≤ 8 |
| `map[K]V` | `Record<string, V>`, `Record<number, V>` for integer keys |
| struct of the package | an `interface` with its name; fields follow the `napi`/`json` tags; pointers, `any` and `omitempty` fields are optional |
| other structs | an inline object type |
| `*T` | `T \| null` (parameters also accept `undefined`) |
| `*T` of a class | `Class \| null` |
| `napi.Either[A, B]` | `A \| B` |
| `any`, `napi.Value` | `any` |
| `napi.Object`, `napi.Function`, `napi.Promise`, … | `object`, `(...args: any[]) => any`, `Promise<any>`, … |
| `error` only / no result | `void`; asynchronous: `Promise<…>` |

The declarations use `Buffer`, declared by `@types/node`.

## Usage

```
napi-go gen [flags]

  -C dir             project (package.json) or Go package directory (default .)
  -name name         base name of the .node files (default: binaryName of package.json, or the directory name)
  -package-name pkg  npm package of the platform packages (default: name of package.json)
  -js file           JS entry point (default index.js; empty: none)
  -dts file          TypeScript declarations (default index.d.ts; empty: none)
  -tags tags         build tags, as for go build
  -check             do not write: fail if the generated files are out of date (for CI)
```

In a project, the files go next to `package.json` and `zz_napi.go` into the Go package
(`napiGo.goPackage`); `go generate` in the Go package finds the `package.json` above it.

The generator uses only the Go standard library. It type-checks the package with the export data
of the Go build cache (`go list -export`), so it needs the same toolchain as the build, C compiler
included.

## What is generated, and what is not

The generated Go code registers the exports with the generic wrappers of package `napi`; the
conversions are the cached codecs of Layer 2. Generating Go conversion code for each struct was
measured and dropped: on a struct of five fields it was 15% faster from JS to Go and no faster from
Go to JS (about 2 µs either way), because the time goes into the Node-API calls for each property,
not into Go. Reading the properties of a struct in one C call is the optimization that would help.

docs.title: napi — Layers 1 and 2 of napi-go
docs.markdown:
# napi — Layers 1 and 2 of napi-go

Idiomatic Go API on top of Node-API, built on Layer 0 (`sys`), in two layers that can be mixed in
the same addon:

- **Layer 2, the framework** (napi-rs style): declare Go functions and types and napi-go converts
  arguments and results, runs async functions in goroutines and backs JS classes with Go
  values. No hand-written callbacks.
- **Layer 1, the core** (node-addon-api style): typed JS values, Go errors converted into JS
  exceptions, callbacks, classes, references and buffers, for full control.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/napi-bindings/napi-go/napi"
)

type User struct {
	Name  string
	Age   int     `napi:"age"`
	Email *string // nullable
}

type Counter struct{ n int }

func (c *Counter) Inc() int { c.n++; return c.n }

func init() {
	napi.Export("add", napi.Func2(func(a, b float64) float64 { return a + b }))
	napi.Export("greet", napi.Func1(func(u User) string { return "hello " + u.Name }))
	napi.Export("load", napi.Async1(func(ctx context.Context, id string) (User, error) {
		return User{Name: id}, nil // runs in a goroutine; JS gets a Promise
	}))
	napi.Export("Counter", napi.NewClass(napi.Ctor0(func() (*Counter, error) { return &Counter{}, nil })).
		Method("inc", napi.Method0((*Counter).Inc)))
}

func main() {}
```

```sh
go build -buildmode=c-shared -o addon.node .
node -e "const a = require('./addon.node'); console.log(a.add(1, 2), a.greet({ name: 'Ann', age: 3 }))"
```

The same addon with Layer 1:

```go
func init() {
	napi.Init(func(env napi.Env, exports napi.Object) (napi.Value, error) {
		add, err := env.NewFunction("add", func(c napi.CallContext) (napi.Value, error) {
			a, err := c.Arg(0).Float64()
			if err != nil {
				return napi.Value{}, err // TypeError ERR_NAPI_NUMBER_EXPECTED in JS
			}
			b, err := c.Arg(1).Float64()
			if err != nil {
				return napi.Value{}, err
			}
			return c.Env().NewFloat64(a + b)
		})
		if err != nil {
			return napi.Value{}, err
		}
		return napi.Value{}, exports.Set("add", add.Value)
	})
}
```

Complete examples: `tests/e2e/addons/framework` (Layer 2), `tests/e2e/addons/napibasic` (Layer 1),
`tests/e2e/addons/napiasync` (concurrency). The node-addon-api test suite ported to napi
(`tests/addonapisuite`) checks that Layer 1 behaves like node-addon-api.

## Layer 2: the framework

Instead of writing the registrations by hand, annotate the declarations (`//napi:export`,
`//napi:class`) and let [`napi-go gen`](../internal/codegen/README.md) generate them together with
the TypeScript declarations.

### Exports

`napi.Export(name, def)` adds an export, created in every env that loads the addon (main thread
and `worker_threads`), in registration order together with `napi.Init` functions. `def` is a
function (`FuncDef`), a class (`*ClassDef[T]`) or a constant (`napi.Const(v)`, converted with
`ToValue`). A type that cannot be converted makes `require()` fail with a TypeError naming the
export, the wrapper and the type, not the first call. `FuncDef.New(env, name)` creates a JS
function at runtime (to return a closure, for instance).

### Wrappers

Generated for 0 to 8 JS parameters (`napi/zz_wrappers.go`, `go generate ./napi`):

| Wrapper | Go function | JS |
|---|---|---|
| `FuncN` | `func(A1…AN) R` | returns the converted `R` |
| `FuncEN` | `func(A1…AN) (R, error)` | returns `R`, or throws the error |
| `ProcN` / `ProcEN` | `func(A1…AN)` / `… error` | returns `undefined` (or throws) |
| `AsyncN` | `func(context.Context, A1…AN) (R, error)` | returns a Promise; the function runs in a goroutine |
| `AsyncProcN` | `func(context.Context, A1…AN) error` | Promise resolved with `undefined` |
| `MethodN`, `MethodEN`, `MethodProcN`, `MethodProcEN` | the same with a `*T` receiver first | methods of the class of `T` |
| `CtorN` | `func(A1…AN) (*T, error)` | constructor of the class of `T` |

A parameter of type `napi.Env` or `napi.CallContext` is filled from the call and does not consume
a JS argument (`Func2(func(env napi.Env, s string) (napi.Value, error))` takes one JS argument).
Missing JS arguments are `undefined`, extra ones are ignored. The JS function has the Go name
given to `Export` and a `length` equal to its JS parameters.

### Type mapping

| Go | JS (from JS) | JS (to JS) |
|---|---|---|
| `bool` | boolean | boolean |
| `float64`, `float32` | number | number |
| `int8`…`int32`, `uint8`…`uint32` | number, **integer in range** (else RangeError `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`, never truncated) | number |
| `int`, `int64`, `uint`, `uint64`, `uintptr` | integer number or BigInt in range | number (beyond 2⁵³ precision is lost: use `*big.Int`) |
| `string` | string | string |
| `[]byte` | Buffer, Uint8Array, Uint8ClampedArray, Int8Array, ArrayBuffer, DataView: **a view** of the JS memory (a copy in `Async*`) | a new Buffer (copy) |
| `*big.Int`, `big.Int` | BigInt or integer number | BigInt |
| `time.Time` | Date (invalid Date: RangeError) | Date |
| `[]T` | array | array (`nil` → `[]`) |
| `[N]T` | array of length N | array |
| `map[K]V` (K string or integer kinds) | object (own enumerable keys) | object, keys sorted |
| struct | object: exported fields, see below | object |
| `*T` | `null`/`undefined` → `nil`, else T | `nil` → `null` |
| `*T` of a registered class | instance of the class (or `null`/`undefined` → `nil`) | its instance |
| `any` | natural type: `nil`, `bool`, `float64`, `string`, `*big.Int`, `time.Time`, `[]byte` (copy), `[]any`, `map[string]any`, `napi.Function` | conversion of the dynamic type |
| `Either[A, B]` | tries A, then B | the value that is set |
| `napi.Value`, `Object`, `Function`, `Array`, `String`, `Buffer`, … | checked and passed as is (not in `Async*`) | as is |
| type implementing `FromJS` / `ToJS` | `(*T).FromJS(v Value) error` | `T.ToJS(env Env) (Value, error)` |

Named types convert like their underlying type (`type Celsius float64`). Not convertible:
channels, functions, complex numbers, non-empty interfaces (from JS), maps with other key types.

**Structs.** The JS name of a field is its `napi` tag, else its `json` tag, else the Go name in
lowerCamelCase (`UserID` → `userID`, `URLPath` → `urlPath`). `napi:"-"` skips the field,
`omitempty` leaves zero values out and makes the field optional. Embedded structs are flattened,
as in `encoding/json`. A field that is `undefined` is an error unless it is optional: a pointer,
`any`, `napi.Value`, or tagged `omitempty`. Recursive types are supported.

**Errors.** A failed conversion throws TypeError `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`, RangeError
`ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` or `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` (the codes Node.js uses for its own argument
checks), with the position of the value:
`argument 1: address.tags[2]: expected string, got number`. Errors returned by the Go function
follow the Layer 1 rules (table below); a panic becomes `GO_PANIC`.

### Classes

```go
napi.Export("Counter", napi.NewClass(napi.Ctor1(newCounter)).
	Method("add", napi.Method1((*Counter).Add)).
	Accessor("value", napi.Accessor(func(c *Counter) int { return c.n }, func(c *Counter, v int) { c.n = v })).
	Static("from", napi.Func1(func(n int) *Counter { return &Counter{n: n} })).
	StaticConst("MAX", 100))
```

Instances wrap a `*T`. Methods and accessors are on the prototype, statics on the constructor.
A `*T` result creates the instance of its class, or returns the existing one: in an env the same
`*T` is always the same JS object. A `*T` parameter accepts only instances of the class. If `*T`
has `Finalize(env napi.Env)`, it runs when the last instance wrapping that `*T` is collected (it
must not call JS). `napi.RegisterClass(name, def)` makes a class known without exporting it;
with the zero `CtorDef` a class cannot be constructed from JS. JS subclasses (`class Sub extends
Counter`) work.

### Async functions and JSFunc

`AsyncN` converts the arguments on the JS thread (so a bad argument throws synchronously), runs
the function in a goroutine (`Env.Async`, with the env context), and converts the result on the
JS thread when the Promise settles. Parameters and results must not contain napi values; `[]byte`
arguments are copied.

`NewJSFunc[A, R](env, fn, opts)` lets goroutines call a JS function and wait for the converted
result: `r, err := f.Call(ctx, arg)`. A returned Promise is awaited; JS exceptions and rejections
become an `*Error` with the JS message, code and kind. It is a threadsafe function (Release,
Abort, Ref/Unref); queued calls return `ErrClosing` when it is aborted and `ErrEnvClosed` when
the env is destroyed.

### How it works, and what it costs

- **Codecs.** Each Go type gets a codec built once with reflection and cached; at run time it
  works on `unsafe` pointers. Primitives, `[]byte`, napi values and class pointers are converted
  by direct calls, so their Go values stay on the stack: **0 Go allocations per call** for
  numbers, booleans, Buffers, methods and accessors (measured in the e2e tests).
- **Typed trampoline.** Functions, methods and accessors use a C trampoline that reads number,
  boolean and string arguments (up to 512 bytes in total), unwraps `this` for methods, and
  creates number, boolean and short string results in C: one cgo transition per call. A value
  C cannot convert (wrong type, long string) is converted in Go, with the same error messages.

  | Call (Node 22, Linux x64) | untyped path | typed path |
  |---|---|---|
  | `add(1, 2)`: `Func2(float64, float64) float64` | 628 ns | 306 ns |
  | `greet("x")`: `Func1(string) string` | 671 ns | 324 ns |
  | `c.add(1)`: `Method1(int) int` | 693 ns | 280 ns |
  | empty function (reference) | 152 ns | |

## Contents

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `env.go` | `Env`, `Init`, per-env state (instance data), versions, `RunScript`, pending exceptions, `ReadStats` |
| `value.go` | `Value`, `Type`, `Is*` predicates, `As*` conversions, primitive getters, coercion |
| `primitive.go` | numbers, booleans, `String` (UTF-8/UTF-16/Latin-1), `Symbol`, `BigInt` (including `*big.Int`), `Date` |
| `object.go` | `Object` and properties (string key, value, index), keys, prototype, freeze/seal, `Array`, `Property` and `DefineProperties` |
| `function.go` | `Callback`, `CallContext`, `Function` (`NewFunction`, `Call`, `New`), callback table |
| `class.go` | `DefineClass`, `Promise`/`Deferred` on the JS thread |
| `dispatcher.go` | per-env dispatcher (one threadsafe function, coalesced Go queue), `Env.Context`, `Ref.DeleteLater` |
| `async.go` | `Env.Async`, `Resolver`: Promises settled from goroutines |
| `tsfn.go` | `ThreadsafeFunction[T]`, `CallMode`, `ErrClosing`, `ErrQueueFull` |
| `lifecycle.go` | finalizers, `Wrap`/`Unwrap`/`UnwrapAs`, type tags (objects and externals), `External`, `Ref`, handle scopes, cleanup hooks |
| `buffer.go` | `Buffer`, `ArrayBuffer` (including external, zero-copy), `TypedArray`, `DataView` |
| `errors.go` | `Error`, `ErrPendingException`, `TypeError`/`RangeError`/`SyntaxError`, `Throw`, throwing rules, `Env.Check` for statuses from `sys` |
| `table.go` | ID → Go value table with lock-free reads |
| `conv.go` | Layer 2: codecs (Go ↔ JS conversions), `ToValue`, `FromValue`, `FromJS`, `ToJS` |
| `either.go` | `Either[A, B]` |
| `export.go` | Layer 2: `FuncDef`, the call engine (`arg`, `result`), `Export`, `Const` |
| `zz_wrappers.go` | generated: `FuncN`, `AsyncN`, `MethodN`, `CtorN` and variants (`internal/genwrappers`) |
| `classdef.go` | Layer 2: `NewClass`, `ClassDef`, `Accessor`, `RegisterClass`, instance identity |
| `typed.go` | Layer 2 on the typed trampoline of `sys` |
| `tsfncall.go` | `JSFunc`: calls from goroutines with a converted result |

## Layer 1: design choices

**Value carries its env.** `Value` is `{env, napi_value}`: two words passed by value, like
`Napi::Value`. Specialized types (`Object`, `Function`, `String`, `Buffer`, ...) embed
`Value`, so they inherit all its methods and `x.Value` returns the generic value without
conversions. Arguments to `Set`, `Call`, and similar methods are `Value` rather than an interface:
converting a struct to an interface would allocate.

**Errors.** Every fallible operation returns `error`. A status other than `napi_ok`
becomes a `*napi.Error` with the message from `napi_get_last_error_info`, copied immediately (Node
overwrites it on the next call). In JS:

| Error returned by a callback | Thrown as |
|---|---|
| `*napi.Error` from a `*_expected` status | `TypeError`, code `ERR_NAPI_<STATUS>` (e.g. `ERR_NAPI_NUMBER_EXPECTED`) |
| `*napi.Error` from another status | `Error`, code `ERR_NAPI_<STATUS>` |
| `napi.TypeError(code, msg)`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError` | the corresponding constructor, with code |
| error implementing `JSCode() string` | `Error` with that code |
| any other `error` | `Error` with message `err.Error()` |
| `napi.Throw(v)` | the value `v` as-is |
| `ErrPendingException` | the already-pending exception, unchanged |
| panic | `Error` with code `GO_PANIC` (handled by `sys`) |

Wrapped errors (`fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`, `errors.Join`) preserve their type and code. If
an exception is already pending, the returned error is ignored: JS receives the first exception.
`Env.Catch(err)` catches the exception signaled by `ErrPendingException` and clears it.

**IDs instead of pointers.** The cgo rules forbid passing Go pointers to C. Callbacks,
values associated via `Wrap` and `NewExternal`, finalizers, and cleanup hooks are stored in two tables
(`callbacks`, `handles`) and Node-API receives an ID as `data`/`hint`. Reads are lock-free (atomic
loads on 256-slot segments); IDs are freed in the finalizer of the JS object holding them and
reused. A function created with `NewFunction` or a class from `DefineClass` keeps its callbacks
alive until V8 garbage-collects it. `ReadStats` exposes the counters (for leak tests).

**Per-env state.** `Init` runs for every env that loads the addon (main thread and `worker_threads`).
The napi state for an env is stored via `napi_set_instance_data` and released when the env is
destroyed; `Env.SetInstanceData` stores the user's value within it. Therefore, an addon using napi
must not call `sys.SetInstanceData` or register `sys` handlers directly.

**Allocations.** Measured in e2e tests: 0 Go allocations per call for a callback,
reading/writing numbers, `typeof`, reading a property by string key (key created
with `node_api_create_property_key_utf8` when available), and `Function.Call` with no arguments.
`GoString` reads strings up to 250 bytes into a stack buffer with a single cgo crossing:
the only allocation is the Go string. `Call` and `New` with arguments allocate the argument buffer
(functions that execute JS cannot be marked `nocallback`, so cgo moves the buffer to the heap).

**Zero-copy buffers.** `Bytes`, `NewBuffer`, `NewArrayBuffer`, and `TypedArray.Info` return
a `[]byte` backed by V8 memory, valid as long as the object is alive and not detached: copy it before
retaining it or passing it to a goroutine. `NewExternalBuffer`/`NewExternalArrayBuffer` hand JS
Go memory pinned with `runtime.Pinner` until the finalizer runs; where external buffers are not
allowed (`napi_no_external_buffers_allowed`: V8 sandbox, Electron) they fall back to a copy.

## Threading

Everything except the APIs listed below must be called on the env's JS thread, inside a callback,
`Init`, or code those run (a `Resolver`, a `callJS`, a finalizer). `Env`, `Value`, and `Ref` must
not be used from other goroutines. To work from goroutines:

| API | Use |
|---|---|
| `Env.Async(work)` | returns a Promise settled by `work`, which runs in a goroutine without `Env` and returns a `Resolver` that builds the result on the JS thread (napi-rs `AsyncTask` / `async fn`). Errors and panics reject it; the event loop stays alive until it settles |
| `Env.Context()` | a `context.Context` canceled when the env is destroyed (worker terminated, process exiting): goroutines started for the env should stop |
| `NewThreadsafeFunction[T](env, fn, callJS, opts)` | goroutines `Call(v T, Blocking/NonBlocking)`; `callJS` converts `v` and calls `fn` on the JS thread (`Napi::TypedThreadSafeFunction`). `Acquire`/`Release`/`Abort` from any goroutine, `Ref`/`Unref` on the JS thread |
| `Ref.DeleteLater()` | deletes a reference from any goroutine (queued on the JS thread) |
| `AsyncN` (Layer 2) | `Env.Async` with automatic conversion of arguments and result |
| `NewJSFunc[A, R]` (Layer 2) | goroutines call a JS function and receive its converted result (`Call(ctx, a)`) |

How it works and what it guarantees:

- **One dispatcher per env.** Each env (main thread, worker) has one `napi_threadsafe_function`,
  unref'd, and a Go queue of closures: a burst of results from goroutines costs one Node-API call
  (the call is made only when the queue goes from empty to non-empty). `Async` keeps the event
  loop alive while work is pending. A closure that throws ends its batch, and the remaining
  closures run on the next call.
- **Destroyed envs.** When the env is destroyed, `Env.Context()` is canceled and pending Promises
  are dropped (nobody can observe them). The methods of a `ThreadsafeFunction` then return
  `ErrClosing`: calls hold a read lock that the finalizer takes for writing, so a goroutine can
  never call a function Node has already freed.
- **Closed functions.** After the last `Release`, or after `Abort`, every method returns
  `ErrClosing`. Node-API itself keeps accepting calls until the JS thread notices, and reports
  `napi_invalid_arg` after an abort.
- **Blocking calls.** Node wakes a thread blocked on a full queue with a single
  `cond->Signal`, and only when it pops from a full queue or closes the function
  (`src/node_api.cc`): with several threads blocked at once, wake-ups are lost. `Call` first tries
  without blocking. If the queue is full, goroutines wait for room one at a time.
- **Errors in `callJS`.** An error or panic in `callJS` is thrown on the JS thread. Node reports
  it as an uncaught exception for modules declaring Node-API 10 (`napi_go_v10`) or with
  `--force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy=true`. Otherwise it emits the DEP0168 warning and
  drops it.

## Current limitations

- With `napi_go_experimental`, finalizers may run inside V8's GC: `FinalizeFunc` callbacks
  must not call functions that execute JS (`node_api_post_finalizer` is not exposed yet).
- `DefineClass` creates base classes: inheriting from a native class works from JS
  (`class Sub extends Counter`), not between classes defined in Go.
- Async context, `MakeCallback` and `napi_async_work` (the libuv thread pool) are available only in
  `sys`; `Env.Async` runs work in goroutines.
- A `ThreadsafeFunction` call does not return the JS result: use `JSFunc` for that.
- Layer 2: no async methods (use `Env.Async` in a method), no variadic Go functions (inject
  `CallContext`), class methods have `length` 0, classes defined in Go cannot extend each other,
  and a `*T` converts to the class registered for `T` only (one class per Go type).
- A class defined with `DefineClass` always throws a TypeError when called without `new`; there
  is no hook to make it act as a factory (node-addon-api's `ObjectWrap::OnCalledAsFunction`).
- `NewSymbol` always sets a description: `Symbol()` without one has no counterpart.
- SharedArrayBuffer creation (experimental Node-API) is not wrapped.

docs.title: sys — Layer 0 of napi-go
docs.markdown:
# sys — Layer 0 of napi-go

1:1 bindings for all Node-API 1–10 functions (154 functions, `node-api-headers` 1.9.0),
generated by `internal/gen`. This is the foundation for Layer 1 (`napi`, Phase 2); use it
directly only when raw ABI access is needed.

```go
func init() {
	sys.SetModuleInitHandler(func(env sys.Env, exports sys.Value) sys.Value {
		var fn sys.Value
		sys.CreateFunction(env, name, sys.AutoLength, sys.CallbackTrampoline, 0, &fn)
		sys.SetNamedProperty(env, exports, name, fn)
		return exports
	})
	sys.SetCallbackHandler(func(env sys.Env, info sys.CallbackInfo, data uintptr, this sys.Value, args []sys.Value) sys.Value {
		// data = 0: the function registered above
	})
}
```

Complete example: `tests/e2e/addons/sysbasic`.

## Structure

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `include/` | vendored Node-API headers (types only) and `symbols.js` |
| `zz_api.h`, `zz_api.c` | *generated*: `gn_api[]` function pointer table and `static inline` C wrappers |
| `zz_api.go` | *generated*: Go wrappers, `Fn` enum, `#cgo noescape` directives |
| `zz_enums.go`, `zz_enums_check.go` | *generated*: Node-API enums and compile-time value checks against the C compiler |
| `zz_nocallback*.go` | *generated*: `#cgo nocallback` directives, per build tag |
| `types.go` | handles, function pointers, mirror structs with compile-time layout checks |
| `handlers.go` | C → Go entry trampolines and handlers, `//export` |
| `version_*.go` | declared Node-API version, per build tag |
| `loader.c` | runtime symbol resolution from the host process (`dlsym` / `GetProcAddress`) |
| `module.c` | `NAPI_MODULE_INIT`: symbol loading, runtime guard, module registration, signal handler repair and `SA_ONSTACK` hook |
| `trampoline.c` | C trampolines (callbacks, finalizers, TSFN, async work, cleanup hooks) |
| `guard.c` | guard against a second Go runtime on the same thread (macOS x64 only) |
| `sigfix.c` | restores `SA_RESETHAND` on `node::SignalExit` (macOS) |
| `typed.c`, `typed.go` | typed callback trampoline for Layer 2: primitive arguments and results converted in C, `this` unwrapped in C, one cgo transition per call |
| `onstack.c` | adds `SA_ONSTACK` to the signal handlers Node/libuv install after the module loads (Linux, GOT hook of `sigaction`) |

To regenerate: `go generate ./sys`. CI verifies that generated files are up to date with
`go run ./internal/gen -check`. Decisions that cannot be inferred from the headers (parameter
overrides, `noescape`/`nocallback`, Go enum names) live in `internal/gen/policy.go`.

## Design Choices

**Runtime-resolved symbols.** No import library and no undefined symbols at link time: the
`.node` binary does not link against `node.exe`/`node` and compiles with `go build`/`go test`
without Node installed. Calling a function missing from the host Node process returns
`StatusUnavailable`; `Available(Fn…)` checks availability in advance. Functions up to the
declared Node-API version are required: if any are missing, module loading fails with
`ERR_NAPI_GO_MISSING_FUNCTIONS`.

**By-value outputs.** cgo avoids moving a Go pointer passed to C onto the heap only if the
function has *both* `noescape` *and* `nocallback`. Functions that may execute JS (getters,
Proxies, `call_function`, ...) cannot be marked `nocallback`, so `&result` would escape to the
heap on every call. Therefore, each C wrapper returns outputs by value in a struct: the Go
signature stays 1:1 (pointers, `nil` = `NULL`), but no Go output pointer crosses cgo.
Measured result in e2e tests: **0 allocations per call**, even for `GetNamedProperty`.

**Opaque data as `uintptr`.** `void*` values retained by Node-API (data, hint, context, ...) are
exposed as `uintptr`: cgo rules forbid handing Go pointers to C for long-term storage, and the
type makes this explicit.

**`noescape` / `nocallback`.** Still useful for input buffers (strings, argument arrays).
`nocallback` is applied only to functions that never execute JS; if one were to re-enter Go, the
Go runtime would terminate the process with an explicit fatal error. With `napi_go_experimental`,
finalizers can run synchronously during V8 GC (verified: all run inside `gc()`), so
`nocallback` is restricted to functions that never allocate on the V8 heap. The cost is
measurable: stack buffers passed to e.g. `GetValueStringUTF8` escape to the heap (1 allocation
per iteration in test benchmarks, vs. 0 with versions 8–10).

## Declared Node-API Version

| Build tag | `DeclaredVersion` | Required functions |
|---|---|---|
| *(none)* | 8 | Node-API 1–8 |
| `napi_go_v9` | 9 | 1–9 |
| `napi_go_v10` | 10 | 1–10 |
| `napi_go_experimental` | `NAPI_VERSION_EXPERIMENTAL` | 1–10 |
| `napi_go_test_version_mismatch` | `NAPI_VERSION_EXPERIMENTAL - 1` | test only: Node.js rejects the module |

`node-api-headers` does not include experimental APIs: `napi_go_experimental` only changes the
declared version (and with it Node's runtime behavior, e.g. synchronous finalizers).
`napi_go_test_version_mismatch` declares a version no Node.js supports and is used solely to
test module rejection (`tests/nodesuite`, test_module_version_mismatch).

An addon that does not register a `ModuleInitHandler` fails to load: `require()` throws
`ERR_NAPI_GO_NO_HANDLER` with Node.js's standard message for a module without an entry point
("Module has no declared entry point.").

## Known Limitations

- **macOS x64: one Go addon per process.** On darwin/amd64 all Go runtimes store `g` in the fixed
  TLS slot `0x30(GS)` (golang/go#23617). `guard.c` rejects entry into a second Go runtime with
  `ERR_NAPI_GO_FOREIGN_RUNTIME` instead of corrupting memory. However, the rejected runtime has
  already initialized and its signal handlers remain installed; this still needs further investigation.
- **musl/Alpine** is unsupported: Go releases (≤ 1.27) cannot load `c-shared` libraries on musl.
- **Windows**: each JS → Go entry costs ~1 µs (missing `x_cgo_bindm` in the Go runtime).

Details and benchmarks: `spike/README.md` (Phase 0). The spike was removed after its tests moved to
`tests/e2e`; its last version is in commit `ad50e4c`.

docs.title: Vendored Node-API Headers
docs.markdown:
# Vendored Node-API Headers

Unmodified copy of `include/*.h` and `symbols.js` from the npm package
[`node-api-headers`](https://github.com/nodejs/node-api-headers) **1.9.0** (MIT license, see `LICENSE`).

- The headers are used for **types** only: functions are called through the generated function
  pointer table (`../zz_api.h`), resolved at runtime from the host process.
- `symbols.js` provides the minimum Node-API version for each function.
- The package does not include experimental APIs (`NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL`).

To update: replace these files with those from a newer version of the package, update the
version number above and in `internal/gen` (`headersVersion`), then run `go generate ./sys`.

docs.title: node-addon-api Test Suite Ported to napi
docs.markdown:
# node-addon-api Test Suite Ported to `napi`

The [node-addon-api](https://github.com/nodejs/node-addon-api) tests for the parts of the C++ API
that Layer 1 (`napi`) covers, with the C++ test binding (`test/binding.cc` and the files it
includes) rewritten in Go on top of `napi`. The JS scripts are node-addon-api's own: when one
passes, the Go binding behaves like the C++ one, including error messages. The few lines changed
for napi-go are marked with a `// napi-go:` comment and listed below.

Source: nodejs/node-addon-api @ `25c6b21`. License of copied files:
[LICENSE.node-addon-api.md](LICENSE.node-addon-api.md) (MIT).

```bash
node tests/addonapisuite/run.mjs                  # build and run everything
node tests/addonapisuite/run.mjs object/           # only tests whose id contains "object/"
node tests/addonapisuite/run.mjs --no-build error
GOEXPERIMENT=cgocheck2 node tests/addonapisuite/run.mjs
NAPI_VERSION=8 node tests/addonapisuite/run.mjs    # declare Node-API 8 instead of Node's version
```

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `run.mjs` | runner: builds `binding/` into `test/build/Release/binding.node`, runs each script in its own process with the flags of node-addon-api's `test/index.js` |
| `binding/` | Go port of the binding: one file per group of C++ files, each saying how C++-only constructs were mapped |
| `test/` | node-addon-api scripts, at their original paths; `common/index.js`, `testUtil.js`, `napi_child.js` and `child_processes/addon_data.js` are the original helpers |
| `index.js` | stand-in for node-addon-api's root `index.js`, read by `test/napi_child.js` |
| `status.json` | skipped scripts with the reason (none at the moment) |

The binding declares the Node-API version of the running Node.js (or `NAPI_VERSION`), as
node-addon-api's `common.gypi` does: the scripts skip the checks for features the version lacks.

## Ported tests (44)

`addon_data`, `array_buffer`, `basic_types/{array,boolean,number,value}`, `bigint`, `buffer`,
`dataview/{dataview,dataview_read_write}`, `date`, `env_cleanup`, `env_misc`, `error`,
`error_handling_for_primitives`, `external`,
`function`, `globalObject/global_object_{delete,get,has_own,set}_property`, `handlescope`,
`memory_management`, `name`, `object/{delete_property,finalizer,get_property,has_own_property,
has_property,object,object_freeze_seal,set_property,subscript_operator}`, `objectwrap`,
`objectwrap_constructor_exception`, `objectwrap_removewrap`, `promise`, `reference`, `run_script`,
`symbol`, `type_taggable`, `typedarray`, `typedarray-bigint`, `version_management`.

## Changes to the scripts

| File | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `test/common/index.js` | `runTest` and `runTestWithBindingPath` load only `binding.node` | the other three bindings are C++ build variants of the same sources (no C++ exceptions, `Napi::Maybe`, a custom namespace) |
| `test/name.js` | `nullStringShouldThrow` assertion removed | it tests node-addon-api's own check in `String::New(env, (const char*)nullptr)`; a Go string cannot be null |
| `test/objectwrap.js` | the 4 `/Invalid argument/` matches also accept `does not wrap a Go value` | unwrapping a non-wrapped object returns `napi.ErrNotWrapped`, whose message is napi's own |

## Not ported

| node-addon-api tests | Reason |
|---|---|
| `async_*`, `threadsafe_function/*`, `typed_threadsafe_function/*`, `callbackscope`, `async_context`, `objectwrap_worker_thread`, `error_terminating_environment` | asynchronous work, threadsafe functions and async contexts: Phase 3 |
| `addon` | `Napi::Addon<T>`, the C++ class-based module definition: the Go counterpart is Layer 2 (Phase 4) |
| `objectwrap_function` | a class called without `new` acting as a factory (`ObjectWrap::OnCalledAsFunction`): `napi.DefineClass` always throws a TypeError, as JS classes do |
| `function_reference`, `object_reference`, `movable_callbacks`, `thunking_manual`, `callbackInfo`, `value_type_cast`, `maybe`, `object/object_deprecated`, `objectwrap_multiple_inheritance`, `except_all` | C++ API surface without a Go counterpart (reference wrapper classes, move semantics, manual thunks, `CallbackInfo::SetData`, `Napi::Maybe`, deprecated property descriptors, C++ multiple inheritance, C++ exceptions) |
| `finalizer_order`, `shared_array_buffer`, `require_basic_finalizers` | experimental Node-API (`node_api_post_finalizer`, SharedArrayBuffer creation) not exposed by `napi` yet |
| `exports`, `addon_build` | node-addon-api's npm package and its node-gyp build, not the C++ API |

docs.title: Node.js Test Suite Ported to sys
docs.markdown:
# Node.js Test Suite Ported to `sys`

The Node.js [`test/js-native-api`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/tree/main/test/js-native-api) and
[`test/node-api`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/tree/main/test/node-api) test suites, with the C
addons rewritten in Go on top of Layer 0 (`sys`). The JS scripts are the original ones,
**unmodified**: if a test passes, the Go addon behaves identically to the C addon, including error
messages.

Source: nodejs/node @ `75191c45afeb`. License of copied files: [LICENSE.nodejs](LICENSE.nodejs) (MIT).

```bash
node tests/nodesuite/run.mjs                    # build and run everything
node tests/nodesuite/run.mjs test_async         # only tests whose id contains "test_async"
node tests/nodesuite/run.mjs --no-build test_number/test_null
GOEXPERIMENT=cgocheck2 node tests/nodesuite/run.mjs
```

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `run.mjs` | runner: builds targets from each `binding.gyp`, runs each `.js` honoring its `// Flags:` and `// Env:` lines |
| `common/` | minimal replacement for Node.js's `test/common` (`mustCall`, `buildType`, `nodeProcessAborted`, …); `require-as.js`, `tick.js`, `tmpdir.js`, `report.js`, `fixtures.js`, `child_process.js`, and `sea.js` are copied verbatim |
| `fixtures/` | `test/fixtures` files used by the scripts (`dotenv/uv-threadpool.env`, `sea/addon/`) |
| `internal/napitest/` | Go equivalent of `common.h` / `common-inl.h` |
| `js-native-api/<test>/`, `node-api/<test>/` | original `binding.gyp` and `*.js` + Go port (`main.go`, …) |
| `status.json` | skipped tests, unconditionally (`skip`), below a Node.js version (`minNodeMajor`, or `minNodeVersion` with a minimum per release line), or on specific platforms (`skipPlatforms`, e.g. `darwin-x64`) |
| `<dir>/napi-go.json` (optional) | extra defines for a target when the C source sets them inline (e.g. `#define NAPI_VERSION 9`) |

Runner rules, modeled after Node.js's `test/testpy`:

- each `.js` file in a test directory is a test (id `suite/dir/file`, without extension);
- a test passes if the process exits with code 0; `1..0 # Skipped` on stdout counts it as skipped;
- for each target in `binding.gyp`, the Go source lives in `<dir>/<target>/`, or directly in `<dir>/`
  when there is only one target; the addon is written to `build/Release/<target>.node`;
- when multiple targets compile the same C source (e.g. with different defines), the port lives in
  `<dir>/internal/<name>/` and each `<target>/main.go` only registers its `Init`; `#if NAPI_VERSION`
  differences branch on `sys.DeclaredVersion`;
- target defines select the `sys` build tag: none → Node-API 8, `NAPI_VERSION=9` → `napi_go_v9`,
  `NAPI_VERSION=10` → `napi_go_v10`, `NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL` → `napi_go_experimental`,
  `NAPI_VERSION=2147483646` → `napi_go_test_version_mismatch` (only `test_module_version_mismatch`);
- a test exceeding 120 s is killed along with all child processes (process group on POSIX,
  `taskkill /T` on Windows) and the report includes `ps` output and, on macOS, thread stack traces
  (`sample`);
- scripts run with `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` and `NODE_OPTIONS` stripped from the runner environment,
  matching Node.js CI (an `// Env:` line can set them again); `tmpdir` uses
  `tests/nodesuite/.tmp.0`.

## Porting a Test

1. Copy `binding.gyp` and all `.js` files in the directory from Node.js without modifying them.
2. Rewrite each C source file in Go preserving names, call order, and assertions.
   The macros in `common.h` have equivalents in `napitest`:

   | C | Go |
   |---|---|
   | `NODE_API_CALL(env, call)` | `if !nt.Call(env, call) { return nil }` |
   | `NODE_API_CALL_RETURN_VOID(env, call)` | `if !nt.Call(env, call) { return }` |
   | `NODE_API_ASSERT(env, cond, msg)` | `if !nt.Assert(env, cond, "<cond as in C>", msg) { return nil }` |
   | `NODE_API_BASIC_CALL_RETURN_VOID(env, call)` | `if !nt.BasicCall(env, call) { return }` (stderr + `abort()`) |
   | `NODE_API_BASIC_ASSERT_RETURN_VOID(cond, msg)` | `if !nt.BasicAssert(cond, "<cond as in C>", msg) { return }` |
   | `assert(expr)` from `<assert.h>`, `abort()` | `nt.CAssert(cond, "<expr as in C>")`, `nt.Abort()` |
   | `NODE_API_ASSERT_STATUS(env, cond, msg)` | `nt.AssertStatus(env, cond, "<cond as in C>", msg)` |
   | `NODE_API_CHECK_STATUS(call)` | `if st := call; st != sys.StatusOK { return st }` |
   | `DECLARE_NODE_API_PROPERTY(name, fn)` | `nt.DeclareProperty(name, fn)` |
   | `napi_define_properties(env, obj, n, descs)` | `nt.DefineProperties(env, obj, descs)` |
   | `add_returned_status`, `add_last_status` | `nt.AddReturnedStatus`, `nt.AddLastStatus` |
   | `NAPI_MODULE(…, Init)`, `NAPI_MODULE_INIT()` | `func init() { nt.ModuleInit(initModule) }` |
   | `{ "n", NULL, fn, NULL, NULL, NULL, attrs, NULL }` | `nt.Method("n", fn, attrs)` |
   | `{ "n", NULL, NULL, get, set, NULL, attrs, NULL }` | `nt.Accessor("n", get, set, attrs)` |
   | `{ "n", NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, v, attrs, NULL }` | `nt.Value("n", v, attrs)` |
   | `napi_wrap(…, finalize_cb, hint, …)` | `cb, hint := nt.Finalizer(fn, hint)` then `sys.Wrap(…, cb, hint, …)` |
   | successful `napi_remove_wrap` | `nt.DiscardFinalizer(hint)`: Node-API will no longer invoke the finalizer |
   | `new MyObject` passed to `napi_wrap` | `cgo.NewHandle(obj)`; `Destructor` calls `Value()` and `Delete()` |
   | `(void*)data` in a finalizer | `nt.Pointer(data)` |
   | `napi_create_async_work(…, Execute, Complete, data, …)` | `sys.CreateAsyncWork(…, sys.AsyncExecuteTrampoline, sys.AsyncCompleteTrampoline, nt.AsyncWorkData(execute, complete, data), …)` |
   | `napi_create_threadsafe_function(…, fin_data, fin_cb, context, call_js, …)` | `callJS, fin, ctx := nt.ThreadsafeFunction(callJs, finCb, context)` then `sys.CreateThreadsafeFunction(…, fin_data, fin, ctx, callJS, …)`; `nt.GetThreadsafeFunctionContext` returns the original context |
   | `napi_add_env_cleanup_hook(env, fn, arg)` | `var hook = nt.RegisterCleanupHook(fn)` at package level, then `sys.AddEnvCleanupHook(env, sys.CleanupHookTrampoline, hook.Arg(arg))` (same value for remove) |
   | `uv_thread_create` / `uv_thread_join`, `uv_sleep`, `uv_hrtime` | `nt.Thread` (`Create`, `Join`), `nt.Sleep`, `nt.HRTime` |
   | `napi_add_async_cleanup_hook(env, fn, arg, &h)` | `var hook = nt.RegisterAsyncCleanupHook(fn)`, then `sys.AddAsyncCleanupHook(env, sys.AsyncCleanupHookTrampoline, hook.Arg(arg), &h)` |
   | `uv_check_*`, `uv_idle_*`, `uv_async_*`, `uv_close`, `uv_queue_work` on the Node loop | `nt.UV*` shim (`uv.go`): handles and requests in C memory (`nt.NewUVHandle`, `nt.NewUVReq`), Go callbacks |

   The condition text passed to `Assert` must be copied verbatim from C: the macro embeds it in the
   error message and the JS scripts match it with regular expressions.
3. libuv utilities used solely as test helpers (`uv_sleep`, `uv_thread_create`, `uv_mutex_*`) are
   replaced with their Go equivalents and noted in the file header comment. Functions that operate
   on the Node.js event loop (handles, `uv_queue_work`) go through the `napitest` shim: `uv_*`
   functions are resolved from the node process just like Node-API functions, and only enum values
   and the leading `data` field of handles and requests (stable in libuv 1.x) are relied on from the
   libuv ABI; sizes come from `uv_handle_size` / `uv_req_size`.

## Unavoidable Differences from C

- The `data` of JS functions created from Go carries the index of the function registered in
  `napitest` (`sys.CallbackTrampoline` dispatch), not the C test's `data`.
- Names passed to property descriptors are shared, never-freed C strings (`nt.CStr`, `nt.UTF16`),
  so descriptors contain no Go pointers.
- An accessor's getter and setter share `data` (as in Node-API): `nt.Accessor` registers the pair
  and dispatch selects the getter for a zero-argument call and the setter for a one-argument call.
  Registry index 0 is reserved so a NULL `data` never invokes a function.
- Functions created repeatedly (factories) are registered once at package level: each `nt.Register`
  appends an entry to the registry.
- C++ classes become Go structs and the native pointer passed to `napi_wrap` / `napi_add_finalizer`
  is a `cgo.Handle`. Structs that C allocates with `malloc` and passes as instance data or
  `finalize_data` (containing only C types such as `napi_ref`) stay in C memory (`nt.Malloc`).
  A finalizer canceled by deleting its reference (`6_object_wrap/nested_wrap`) is never called and
  its `nt.Finalizer` handle remains allocated, just like the memory in the C test.
- A TSFN context is a `napitest` token and is never released: Node-API calls `call_js_cb` with a
  NULL env for items remaining in the queue even after `thread_finalize_cb` and does not signal when
  it is done. `thread_finalize_cb` receives the original context as its hint.
- Finalizers go through `sys.FinalizeTrampoline`: `nt.Finalizer(fn, hint)` returns the callback/hint
  pair to pass instead of the C pair, and `fn` receives Node-API's `finalize_data` and the original
  hint. Memory that Node-API must be able to access after the call returns (external strings and
  ArrayBuffers) is allocated with `nt.Malloc` and freed with `nt.Free` / `nt.FreeAddr`. `nt.Malloc`
  never returns NULL for a non-zero size: if allocation fails it aborts the process with a message,
  because the C tests use the result of `malloc` without checking it.

## Status

| Suite | Ported tests |
|---|---|
| js-native-api | all 32: 2_function_arguments, 3_callbacks, 4_object_factory, 5_function_factory, 6_object_wrap, 7_factory_wrap, 8_passing_wrapped, test_array, test_bigint, test_cannot_run_js, test_constructor, test_conversions, test_dataview, test_date, test_error, test_exception, test_finalizer, test_function, test_general, test_handle_scope, test_instance_data, test_new_target, test_number, test_object, test_promise, test_properties, test_reference, test_reference_double_free, test_sharedarraybuffer, test_string, test_symbol, test_typedarray |
| node-api | all 28: 1_hello_world, test_async, test_async_cleanup_hook, test_callback_scope, test_init_order, test_module_version_mismatch, test_null_init, test_uv_loop, test_async_context, test_buffer, test_cleanup_hook, test_env_teardown_gc, test_exception, test_fatal, test_fatal_exception, test_general, test_instance_data, test_make_callback, test_make_callback_recurse, test_reference_by_node_api_version, test_sea_addon, test_threadsafe_function, test_threadsafe_function_abort, test_threadsafe_function_shutdown, test_uv_threadpool_size, test_worker_buffer_callback, test_worker_terminate, test_worker_terminate_finalization |

The scripts come from nodejs/node `main`, so some exercise recent features: `status.json` skips
them below the Node.js version that introduced them. `minNodeMajor` suffices when a feature ships in
a major release; when it is backported to different minors across release lines, `minNodeVersion`
lists the first release in each line (e.g. `22.23.3`, `24.16.0`, `26.1.0`): lines without a
minimum, unless newer than all listed lines, lack the feature. Minimums are derived from
nodejs/node release tags.

On macOS x64 napi-go supports only one Go runtime per process (see known limitations in
`sys/README.md`): scripts that load two addons in the same process
(`js-native-api/test_cannot_run_js`, `node-api/test_reference_by_node_api_version`) are listed in
`skipPlatforms` for `darwin-x64`. On other platforms they run normally.

### Experimental APIs

Six functions used by the tests are not in `sys`'s headers (node-api-headers 1.9.0).
`napitest` resolves them from the node process, just like `sys/loader.c`:

| Function | Used by | If not exported by the running Node |
|---|---|---|
| `node_api_post_finalizer` | test_general/testFinalizer, test_finalizer | error `napitest: Node-API function not exported…` |
| `node_api_is_sharedarraybuffer` | test_dataview, test_sharedarraybuffer | same as above |
| `node_api_create_sharedarraybuffer` | test_sharedarraybuffer | same as above |
| `node_api_create_external_sharedarraybuffer` | node-api/test_buffer | same as above; the env-less finalizer goes through a C trampoline in `napitest` (`noenv.c`) |
| `node_api_set_prototype` | test_general | `Object.setPrototypeOf` |
| `node_api_create_object_with_properties` | test_object | `Object.create` + `napi_set_property` |

For the last two, the fallback using stable APIs has the same observable effect in the scripts; it
exists only to keep the rest of `test_object` and `test_general` running on Node.js versions that do
not export them yet.
