| `macos-arm64-debug` | `unix-debug` | Apple clang |
| `windows-x64-zig-debug` | `windows-zig-debug` | zig cc |
| `windows-x64-zig-release` | `windows-zig-release` | zig cc |

The Linux and macOS jobs without sanitizers also run the `node_parity_*`
tests under Node.js 22. Each job uploads its CTest log as an artifact.

docs.title: Compatibility with Node.js
docs.markdown:
# Compatibility with Node.js

quickjs-napi reproduces the Node-API behaviour of **Node.js 22.23.4**: same
statuses, same pending exceptions, same error codes and messages, same
finalizer ordering. This page lists every known difference, so that addon
authors know what to expect. Each item links to the function reference.

- [Deviations in the API](#deviations-in-the-api)
- [Differences that come from QuickJS](#differences-that-come-from-quickjs)
- [Behaviour that is defined here but not in Node.js](#behaviour-that-is-defined-here-but-not-in-nodejs)
- [Not provided](#not-provided)
- [The executable](#the-executable)

## Deviations in the API

| Function | Node.js 22 | quickjs-napi | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `napi_define_class` | prototype methods have a V8 *signature*: calling one on a foreign object throws `TypeError: Illegal invocation` | the callback runs; it must validate `this` (e.g. with `napi_unwrap`) | [functions.md](node-api/functions.md#napi_define_class) |
| `napi_is_array` | `false` for every Proxy | `true` for a Proxy whose target is an array (as `Array.isArray`); `false` for a revoked Proxy | [values.md](node-api/values.md#napi_is_array) |
| `napi_create_buffer` | memory uninitialized | memory zero-filled | [node-specific.md](node-api/node-specific.md#napi_create_buffer) |
| `node_api_create_buffer_from_arraybuffer`, range out of bounds | `napi_ok` with the `RangeError` pending | `napi_pending_exception` with the same `RangeError` pending | [node-specific.md](node-api/node-specific.md#node_api_create_buffer_from_arraybuffer) |
| `napi_create_typedarray` / `napi_get_typedarray_info` with `napi_float16_array` | `napi_invalid_arg` | supported (QuickJS has `Float16Array`) | [binary-data.md](node-api/binary-data.md#typedarray) |
| `napi_get_typedarray_info`, out-of-bounds non-detached view of a resizable buffer | reports the stored byte offset | reports byte offset 0 (QuickJS does not expose it) | [binary-data.md](node-api/binary-data.md#napi_get_typedarray_info) |
| `napi_get_threadsafe_function_context` with `NULL` arguments | aborts | `napi_invalid_arg` | [async.md](node-api/async.md#napi_get_threadsafe_function_context) |
| `napi_module_register` outside of an addon load | registers a module | prints a warning and does nothing (use `qjsnapi_init_static_addon`) | [environment.md](node-api/environment.md#napi_module_register) |

## Differences that come from QuickJS

| Area | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Finalizer timing** | QuickJS frees an object as soon as its last reference goes away (cycles at `JS_RunGC`). Finalizers therefore usually run **earlier** than in Node.js, at the next loop iteration instead of at some later major GC. Code that assumes an object stays alive while only weakly referenced still works within the same macrotask (the kept-objects list), but not across macrotasks. See [architecture.md](architecture.md#object-lifetime). |
| **BigInt size** | at most 2^20 bits (16384 words; V8: 2^30). `napi_create_bigint_words` beyond that throws `RangeError: Maximum BigInt size exceeded`, as V8 does past its own limit. |
| **BigInt words** | `napi_*_bigint_words` convert through a hexadecimal string: O(n), slower than V8's direct access for very large values. |
| **External strings** | `node_api_create_external_string_*` always copy and run the finalizer immediately (`*copied = true`). Node.js does the same when V8 uses the pointer-compression sandbox, so addons handle it already. |
| **Property keys** | `node_api_create_property_key_*` create ordinary strings: QuickJS atomizes keys itself. Not observable. |
| **External memory** | `napi_adjust_external_memory` keeps the counter but does not influence garbage collection: QuickJS has no such heuristic. |
| **Basic finalizers** | all finalizers run outside the GC, so calling any Node-API function from a `node_api_basic_finalize` never triggers Node's fatal "Finalizer is calling a function that may affect GC state" error. |
| **Async context** | there is no `async_hooks`: `napi_async_init`, `napi_make_callback` and callback scopes work, but no async resource is tracked (`AsyncLocalStorage` and async stack traces do not follow native callbacks). |

## Behaviour that is defined here but not in Node.js

These cases are undefined behaviour or leaks in Node.js; quickjs-napi chose a
safe behaviour:

| Case | quickjs-napi |
|---|---|
| `napi_delete_async_work` on a queued item | the item is freed after its `complete` has run |
| async work items and user references never deleted | freed with the env at teardown (Node.js leaks them) |
| a user `napi_ref` whose finalizer ran but that the addon never deleted | freed at teardown |
| a handle scope left open by a function called from JavaScript | closed with the call's implicit scope (warning in Debug builds) |

## Not provided

- `NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL` APIs: the bundled headers stop at version 10 and
  declare no experimental function (`node_api_post_finalizer`, ...); an addon
  that needs one fails to load because the symbol is missing.
- `napi_would_deadlock` is never returned (Node.js 22 does not return it
  either); a blocking call of a full thread-safe function from the loop
  thread deadlocks.

## The executable

The `quickjs-napi` executable is not Node.js; it provides what addon packages
and their tests need ([host.md](host.md)). In particular:

- `process.version` is `v22.23.4` (the reproduced Node-API behaviour) but
  `process.versions.node` is not set;
- CommonJS only: no ES modules, no `package.json` `"exports"` maps;
- no `worker_threads`, `async_hooks`, `domain`, `fs`, `net`, `http`,
  `crypto`;
- `child_process` without a shell, and an asynchronous child's stdin is never
  a pipe.

docs.title: Embedding API (qjsnapi.h)
docs.markdown:
# Embedding API (`qjsnapi.h`)

The library `qjsnapi` can be embedded in any application that uses QuickJS.
`include/qjsnapi.h` is its whole public interface besides Node-API itself.
The `quickjs-napi` executable ([host.md](host.md)) is one such embedder, and
`test/unit/test_embed.c` is a complete, tested example.

- [Lifecycle at a glance](#lifecycle-at-a-glance)
- [Minimal embedder](#minimal-embedder)
- [Function reference](#function-reference)
- [Embedder responsibilities](#embedder-responsibilities)
- [Linking](#linking)

## Lifecycle at a glance

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant E as embedder
    participant Q as QuickJS
    participant H as qjsnapi host
    participant U as libuv loop
    E->>Q: JS_NewRuntime, JS_NewContext
    E->>H: qjsnapi_host_create(ctx) (or _with_loop)
    E->>H: set_uncaught_handler, set_checkpoint (optional)
    E->>H: qjsnapi_load_addon / qjsnapi_init_static_addon
    H-->>E: exports
    E->>Q: run scripts that use the exports
    E->>U: uv_run(qjsnapi_host_get_loop(host), UV_RUN_DEFAULT)
    U->>H: async work, thread-safe functions, finalizers
    E->>Q: JS_FreeValue(exports)
    E->>H: qjsnapi_host_destroy (cleanup hooks, drain, finalizers)
    E->>Q: JS_FreeContext, JS_FreeRuntime
```

The rules are:

- **One host per `JSContext`.** The host is stored as the context opaque
  (`JS_SetContextOpaque`), so the embedder must not use that slot for anything
  else. `qjsnapi_host_from_context` gets it back.
- **One thread.** The context and the loop run on the same thread. Other
  threads only reach the host through thread-safe functions and async work.
- **Destroy before `JS_FreeContext`.** `qjsnapi_host_destroy` still needs the
  context to finalize references.

## Minimal embedder

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <uv.h>

#include "qjsnapi.h"
#include "quickjs.h"

static void on_uncaught(qjsnapi_host *host, JSContext *ctx, JSValue exc,
                        void *opaque) {
  (void)host;
  (void)opaque;
  const char *s = JS_ToCString(ctx, exc);
  fprintf(stderr, "uncaught: %s\n", s ? s : "?");
  JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
  JS_FreeValue(ctx, exc); /* the handler owns the exception */
}

int main(void) {
  JSRuntime *rt = JS_NewRuntime();
  JSContext *ctx = JS_NewContext(rt);
  qjsnapi_host *host = qjsnapi_host_create(ctx);
  if (!host) return 1;
  qjsnapi_host_set_uncaught_handler(host, on_uncaught, NULL);

  JSValue exports;
  if (qjsnapi_load_addon(host, "./build/Release/addon.node", &exports) < 0) {
    JSValue exc = JS_GetException(ctx); /* the load error is pending */
    on_uncaught(host, ctx, exc, NULL);
  } else {
    JSValue global = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx);
    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "addon", exports); /* takes ownership */
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, global);

    JSValue r = JS_Eval(ctx, "addon.hello()", 13, "<main>",
                        JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
    if (JS_IsException(r)) on_uncaught(host, ctx, JS_GetException(ctx), NULL);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, r);
  }

  /* Async work, thread-safe functions and finalizers run from the loop. */
  uv_run(qjsnapi_host_get_loop(host), UV_RUN_DEFAULT);

  qjsnapi_host_destroy(host);
  JS_FreeContext(ctx);
  JS_FreeRuntime(rt);
  return 0;
}
```

An addon linked into the application instead of loaded from a file:

```c
static napi_value Init(napi_env env, napi_value exports) {
  /* ... napi_define_properties(env, exports, ...) ... */
  return exports;
}

JSValue exports;
if (qjsnapi_init_static_addon(host, "my-static-addon", Init,
                              10 /* module API version */, &exports) < 0) {
  /* exception pending on ctx */
}
```

## Function reference

### Host lifecycle

#### `qjsnapi_host_create`

```c
qjsnapi_host *qjsnapi_host_create(JSContext *ctx);
```

Creates the Node-API host for `ctx`, with a **libuv loop of its own** that
`qjsnapi_host_destroy` closes. It captures the builtins Node-API needs,
evaluates the embedded `Buffer` class, probes the builtin class IDs and
registers the library's loop handles. Must be called before any user script
runs (see [captured builtins](architecture.md#captured-builtins)).
Returns `NULL` on failure; a JavaScript exception may then be pending.

#### `qjsnapi_host_create_with_loop`

```c
qjsnapi_host *qjsnapi_host_create_with_loop(JSContext *ctx,
                                            struct uv_loop_s *loop);
```

Same, on the embedder's loop. The loop must outlive the host and run on the
thread that owns `ctx`. The host adds its handles to it and removes them in
`qjsnapi_host_destroy`, but does not close the loop.

#### `qjsnapi_host_get_loop`

```c
struct uv_loop_s *qjsnapi_host_get_loop(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

The loop of the host: the one `napi_get_uv_event_loop` returns to addons and
the one the embedder must run.

#### `qjsnapi_host_from_context`

```c
qjsnapi_host *qjsnapi_host_from_context(JSContext *ctx);
```

The host attached to `ctx`, or `NULL`. Useful in native functions of the
embedder that only receive a `JSContext`.

#### `qjsnapi_host_destroy`

```c
void qjsnapi_host_destroy(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

Tears down every env as Node.js does at exit, with JavaScript disabled:

1. cleanup hooks, newest first (thread-safe functions start closing, async
   cleanup hooks start);
2. queued async work cancelled;
3. the loop runs until in-flight work, thread-safe functions and async cleanup
   hooks are done;
4. references and instance data finalized;
5. the module cache released and the host detached from the context.

The embedder closes its own handles on the loop first. Must be called before
`JS_FreeContext()`. The full order is described in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#teardown).

### Loading addons

#### `qjsnapi_load_addon`

```c
int qjsnapi_load_addon(qjsnapi_host *host, const char *path, JSValue *exports);
```

Loads a `.node` shared library and runs its Node-API initializer.

- Returns `0` and stores a **new reference** to the exports in `*exports`; the
  caller frees it.
- Returns `-1` with a JavaScript exception pending on the context. Its `code`
  property is `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (the path cannot be resolved) or
  `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` (the library cannot be opened, does not register a
  module, or needs a Node-API version above 10). A legacy module registered
  without an init function fails with `Module has no declared entry point.`
  and no code, as in Node.js. An exception thrown by the initializer is left
  pending as it is.
- Like `process.dlopen`, **every call runs the initializer again** with a new
  env and returns new exports. Caching by path is the module loader's job.
- Fails while the host is being destroyed.

The entry point is resolved as described in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#loading-addons).

#### `qjsnapi_init_static_addon`

```c
int qjsnapi_init_static_addon(qjsnapi_host *host, const char *name,
                              napi_addon_register_func init,
                              int32_t module_api_version, JSValue *exports);
```

Runs the initializer of an addon **linked statically** into the embedder, as
if it had been loaded from `name`. `module_api_version` follows the
`node_api_module_get_api_version_v1` rules: `0` selects the default (8), a
value above 10 fails. Unlike `qjsnapi_load_addon`, the exports are **cached by
name**: a second call with the same name returns a new reference to the same
exports object without running `init` again. `node_api_get_module_file_name`
reports `name` for such an addon.

### Buffer and versions

#### `qjsnapi_host_get_buffer`

```c
JSValue qjsnapi_host_get_buffer(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

The minimal Node.js `Buffer` constructor used by `napi_create_buffer*`
(`Buffer.from`, `alloc`, `toString`, ...; see
[buffers](node-api/node-specific.md#buffers)). The library **does not install it
as a global**: the embedder decides where it is visible (the executable sets
`globalThis.Buffer` and `require('buffer')`). Returns a new reference.

#### `qjsnapi_node_version`

```c
const napi_node_version *qjsnapi_node_version(void);
```

What `napi_get_node_version` reports: `22.23.4`, the Node.js release whose
Node-API behaviour is reproduced, with release name `"quickjs-napi"`. A host
that provides `process` should report the same in `process.version`.

#### `qjsnapi_napi_version`

```c
uint32_t qjsnapi_napi_version(void);
```

The highest Node-API version supported by this build (`10`), the value of
`napi_get_version`.

### Finalizers and weak references

#### `qjsnapi_host_run_finalizers`

```c
size_t qjsnapi_host_run_finalizers(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

Runs the queued finalizers of every env (objects collected by the GC that
have a `napi_wrap`, `napi_add_finalizer`, external value, external
ArrayBuffer or external Buffer finalizer) and returns how many ran. The
library's `uv_check` handle already calls it once per loop iteration, so an
embedder that runs the host's loop does not need to; an embedder with its own
scheduling calls it outside of any JavaScript call. Finalizers still queued at
`qjsnapi_host_destroy` run then, with JavaScript disabled.

#### `qjsnapi_host_has_pending_finalizers`

```c
int qjsnapi_host_has_pending_finalizers(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

Non-zero while finalizers are queued: an event loop that decides itself when
to stop must not exit yet.

#### `qjsnapi_host_clear_kept_objects`

```c
void qjsnapi_host_clear_kept_objects(qjsnapi_host *host);
```

Releases the *kept objects*: the targets of references that became weak,
held strongly until now to reproduce V8's "alive until the next GC" (see
[architecture.md](architecture.md#kept-objects)). The library clears the list
at each of its own checkpoints. The embedder calls it **at the end of each
macrotask it runs itself** (a timer, an I/O callback) and **before an
explicit garbage collection** (`JS_RunGC`), otherwise weakly referenced
objects are collected later than expected.

### Callbacks of the embedder

#### `qjsnapi_host_set_uncaught_handler`

```c
typedef void (*qjsnapi_uncaught_fn)(qjsnapi_host *host, JSContext *ctx,
                                    JSValue exception, void *opaque);
void qjsnapi_host_set_uncaught_handler(qjsnapi_host *host,
                                       qjsnapi_uncaught_fn fn, void *opaque);
```

Called with an exception that no JavaScript frame can catch: thrown by a
finalizer, an async work `complete` callback, a thread-safe function's
`call_js_cb`, a promise job run by the default checkpoint, or passed to
`napi_fatal_exception`. Node.js emits `process.on('uncaughtException')` or
exits. **The handler takes ownership of `exception`.** Without a handler, and
always during `qjsnapi_host_destroy`, the exception is printed on stderr
(`quickjs-napi: uncaught exception in a Node-API callback: ...`) and dropped.

#### `qjsnapi_host_set_checkpoint`

```c
typedef void (*qjsnapi_checkpoint_fn)(qjsnapi_host *host, JSContext *ctx,
                                      void *opaque);
void qjsnapi_host_set_checkpoint(qjsnapi_host *host, qjsnapi_checkpoint_fn fn,
                                 void *opaque);
```

Called after native code entered from the loop (async work completion,
thread-safe function calls, finalizers) and when the outermost callback scope
closes with no JavaScript below it: where Node.js runs its tick and microtask
queues and reports unhandled rejections. The default runs the pending promise
jobs (`JS_ExecutePendingJob`) and reports their exceptions to the uncaught
handler. An embedder with a `process.nextTick` queue or rejection tracking
installs its own (the executable does: `host_checkpoint` in `host/main.c`).

#### `qjsnapi_host_set_force_uncaught_exceptions_policy`

```c
void qjsnapi_host_set_force_uncaught_exceptions_policy(qjsnapi_host *host,
                                                       int force);
```

Node's `--force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy` (default off). When off,
an exception thrown by a thread-safe function callback of an addon built for
Node-API < 10 becomes a `DEP0168` deprecation warning instead of an uncaught
exception. When on, it is always an uncaught exception.

## Embedder responsibilities

| Responsibility | How |
|---|---|
| Run the loop | `uv_run(qjsnapi_host_get_loop(host), ...)`; it runs async work completions, thread-safe function calls and queued finalizers. |
| Report uncaught exceptions | `qjsnapi_host_set_uncaught_handler`. |
| Drain the embedder's own queues | `qjsnapi_host_set_checkpoint` (microtasks, `nextTick`, unhandled rejections). |
| End macrotasks | `qjsnapi_host_clear_kept_objects` after each macrotask it runs itself, and before `JS_RunGC`. |
| Expose `Buffer` | `qjsnapi_host_get_buffer`, if scripts should see it. |
| Cache modules | `qjsnapi_load_addon` never caches; `require` does. |
| Tear down in order | close the embedder's handles, `qjsnapi_host_destroy`, then `JS_FreeContext`, `JS_FreeRuntime`. |
| Export the symbols | addons resolve `napi_*` and `uv_*` from the process (see below). |

## Linking

Addons do not link against the library: they find `napi_*` and `uv_*` in the
process. The executable that embeds the library must therefore **export**
them:

| Platform | What is needed |
|---|---|
| Linux, BSD | link the library as a whole archive and export dynamic symbols (`--export-dynamic`, CMake `ENABLE_EXPORTS`). |
| macOS | whole archive (`-force_load`); addons are linked with `-undefined dynamic_lookup`. |
| Windows (MinGW) | whole archive; the definitions carry `__declspec(dllexport)` (`NAPI_EXTERN`; libuv is built with `BUILDING_UV_SHARED`). node-gyp addons import from `node.exe` and are redirected to the running process by node-gyp's delay-load hook. |

`CMakeLists.txt` does all of this for the `quickjs-napi` target; an embedder
can copy that setup. `tools/check_exports.py <executable>` verifies that every
Node-API function is exported.

Link with `uv_a` (libuv) and the QuickJS library the headers in `include/`
were taken from.

### From a release package

The [release packages](building.md#release-packages) install a CMake
package:

```cmake
find_package(qjsnapi CONFIG REQUIRED)   # CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<package dir>
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE qjsnapi::static)   # or qjsnapi::shared
```

| Target | What it is |
|---|---|
| `qjsnapi::static` | `libqjsnapi.a` + the bundled `libqjs.a` and `libuv.a`, with their system libraries |
| `qjsnapi::core` | `libqjsnapi.a` alone, to link **your own** QuickJS and libuv |
| `qjsnapi::quickjs`, `qjsnapi::uv` | the bundled `libqjs.a` and `libuv.a` |
| `qjsnapi::shared` | the shared library (`libqjsnapi.so`, `libqjsnapi.dylib`, `qjsnapi.dll`) |
| `qjsnapi::addon` | usage requirements of a `.node` addon for the `quickjs-napi` executable |
| `qjsnapi::quickjs-napi` | the executable |

`test/package/CMakeLists.txt` uses each of them; it is what the release
workflow runs on every package.

**Static: three archives.** QuickJS and libuv are separate archives so that
an embedder can replace them (`qjsnapi::core` plus its own libraries). The
replacements must be ABI-compatible with the headers of the package: the same
QuickJS release (`quickjs.h` defines the layout of `JSValue`) and a libuv 1.x
not older than the bundled one (`BUILDINFO.txt` has both versions). The rules
of the table above still apply: to load addons, the executable must link
`libqjsnapi.a` and libuv as whole archives and export their symbols.

**Shared.** The shared library contains QuickJS and libuv and exports
`napi_*`, `uv_*`, `qjsnapi_*` and the QuickJS API (`JS_*`, `js_*`). Create the
`JSRuntime` and `JSContext` with the QuickJS **of the library**: do not link
another QuickJS in the same process (two copies do not share class IDs and
atoms, and values cannot cross between them). Limits:

- **Windows:** node-gyp addons import Node-API from `node.exe`, and their
  delay-load hook redirects that to the *executable* of the process, not to
  `qjsnapi.dll`: they cannot load in a program that uses the DLL. Use the
  static archives (exporting the symbols from the executable, as above), or
  `quickjs-napi.exe`. Addons linked against `libqjsnapi.dll.a` instead load
  normally.
- **Linux, BSD, macOS:** addons find the symbols in the shared library, which
  is loaded globally with the executable; nothing else is needed.

docs.title: The quickjs-napi executable
docs.markdown:
# The `quickjs-napi` executable `quickjs-napi` is a small Node.js-like runtime built on the library. It runs CommonJS scripts, loads `.node` addons with `require`, and provides the subset of Node.js that addon packages and their tests need. It is also the reference embedder of the library ([embedding.md](embedding.md)). Sources: `host/main.c` (command line, event loop, natives), `host/bootstrap.js` (module loader, `process`, builtin modules; embedded in the executable at build time by `cmake/embed.cmake`) and `host/spawn.c` (child processes). - [Command line](#command-line) - [Modules](#modules) - [Globals](#globals) - [Builtin modules](#builtin-modules) - [Event loop](#event-loop) - [Errors and exit](#errors-and-exit) - [Not supported](#not-supported) ## Command line ```sh quickjs-napi [options] script.js [args...] quickjs-napi [options] -e [args...] ``` | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `-e`, `--eval ` | run `code` instead of a script; `process.argv` is `[execPath, args...]` | | `-r`, `--require ` | load the module before the script; repeatable | | `--force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy[=true\|false]` | report exceptions from thread-safe function callbacks of Node-API < 10 addons as uncaught instead of a `DEP0168` warning (see [async.md](node-api/async.md#exceptions-in-call_js_cb)) | | `--no-force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy` | the default | | `--expose-gc` | accepted and ignored: `gc()` is always defined | - `NODE_OPTIONS` is read first, with the same options separated by spaces. Options only Node.js knows are **ignored** there, because the variable is shared with Node.js (a test that sets `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=…` for its children still works). - On the command line an unknown option exits with code **9**, as in Node.js. - Without a script or `-e`, the usage is printed and the exit code is 2. Examples: ```sh quickjs-napi app.js --verbose quickjs-napi -e "console.log(require('./build/Release/addon.node').hello())" quickjs-napi -r ./setup.js test.js NODE_OPTIONS="--require ./setup.js" quickjs-napi test.js ``` ## Modules The script runs as a **CommonJS module**: `require`, `module`, `exports`, `__filename` and `__dirname` are defined as in Node.js. `require(id)` resolves like Node.js for what addon packages use: 1. builtin modules (`require('buffer')`, ...); 2. relative (`./`, `../`) and absolute paths, trying the exact name, then the extensions `.js`, `.json`, `.node`; 3. directories: `package.json` `"main"`, then `index.js`, `index.json`, `index.node`; 4. `node_modules` directories, from the requiring module's directory up to the root. | Extension | Loaded as | |---|---| | `.js` | CommonJS module, wrapped in a function like Node.js | | `.json` | parsed JSON | | `.node` | Node-API addon through [`qjsnapi_load_addon`](embedding.md#qjsnapi_load_addon) | Modules are cached by resolved path (`require.cache`); deleting a cache entry and requiring the addon again runs its initializer again with a new env, like `process.dlopen`. `module.registerBuiltin(name, exports)` is a quickjs-napi extension that lets a script provide a builtin module (the test harnesses use it to provide `assert`). ## Globals | Global | Notes | |---|---| | `process` | `argv`, `env` (the real environment, passed to children), `platform`, `execPath`, `version` (`v22.23.4`, the Node.js release whose Node-API behaviour is reproduced), `release.name` (`quickjs-napi`), `versions.quickjs`, `versions.napi`, `exitCode`, `exit()`, `cwd()`, `nextTick()`, `on`/`once`/`off`/`addListener`/`removeListener`/`listeners`/`emit` for `exit`, `beforeExit`, `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` | | `global` | `globalThis` | | `gc()` | runs the QuickJS GC twice (cycles are collected after weak entries are dropped) and clears the kept objects | | `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval`, `setImmediate`, `clearImmediate`, `queueMicrotask` | timers return objects with `ref()`, `unref()`, `hasRef()` | | `Buffer` | the library's minimal Buffer ([node-specific.md](node-api/node-specific.md#buffers)) | | `console` | `log` from quickjs-libc, plus `error`, `warn`, `info` | | `print`, `scriptArgs` | quickjs-libc helpers | `process.versions.node` is deliberately **not** set, so that packages do not take quickjs-napi for Node.js itself. ## Builtin modules Minimal subsets, providing what addon packages and the test suites use: | Module | Provides | |---|---| | `module` | `builtinModules`, `createRequire`, `registerBuiltin` | | `timers` | the timer functions | | `timers/promises` | `setTimeout`, `setImmediate` returning promises | | `buffer` | `Buffer`, `kMaxLength` | | `util` | `promisify`, `types` (`isArrayBuffer`, `isSharedArrayBuffer`, `isAnyArrayBuffer`, `isArrayBufferView`, `isTypedArray`, `isDataView`, `isDate`, `isPromise`, `isRegExp`, `isNativeError`, ...) | | `url` | `pathToFileURL`, `fileURLToPath` | | `vm` | `runInNewContext(code)`: evaluates in a new realm of the same runtime | | `child_process` | `spawnSync` and `spawn` (below) | | `events` | a minimal `EventEmitter` | ### `child_process` Children are started directly, **without a shell**, with libuv's `uv_spawn` (`host/spawn.c`): - `spawnSync(file, args, options)` runs the child on a private libuv loop until it exits and its pipes are drained. Options: `env`, `cwd`, `stdio` (`'pipe'`, `'inherit'`, `'ignore'`), `input`, `encoding`, `timeout` (the child is killed with `killSignal`, `SIGTERM` by default, and `error.code` is `ETIMEDOUT`). The result has `pid`, `status`, `signal`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `output` and `error` (`ENOENT` when the program does not exist). - `spawn(file, args, options)` runs the child on the main loop and returns a `ChildProcess`-like emitter: `stdout`/`stderr` streams with `data` events and `setEncoding`, then `exit` and `close` events, `kill(signal)`, and an `error` event when it cannot start. An asynchronous child's stdin is never a pipe: it reads end-of-file. Every child of the test suites is the same executable (`process.execPath`), so the tests that spawn processes run on every platform. ## Event loop The executable runs the host's libuv loop (`uv_run`) until nothing referenced is left, then emits `beforeExit` (whose listeners may schedule more work, in which case the loop runs again), then `exit`. ```mermaid flowchart LR T["timers phase
g_timer: due JS timers,
one at a time"] --> P["poll (I/O)
async work completions,
thread-safe functions,
child processes"] P --> C["check phase
g_check: immediates queued before it started
library: queued finalizers"] C --> T CB["after every callback:
checkpoint"] -.-> T CB -.-> P CB -.-> C ``` | Handle | Purpose | |---|---| | `g_timer` (`uv_timer_t`) | armed by `bootstrap.js` for the earliest JavaScript timer; referenced only while a referenced timer exists | | `g_check` (`uv_check_t`, unreferenced) | runs the immediates queued before the check phase began, one at a time | | `g_idle` (`uv_idle_t`) | active while immediates are queued (referenced only for referenced ones), so the poll phase does not block | | library handles | queued finalizers, async work, thread-safe functions ([architecture.md](architecture.md#the-event-loop)) | After **every** callback (a timer, an immediate, an I/O event, a Node-API callback from the loop) a **checkpoint** runs: the promise jobs and `process.nextTick` callbacks, then the unhandled rejections, repeated until both are empty. The same function is installed as the library's checkpoint (`qjsnapi_host_set_checkpoint`), so Node-API callbacks behave like Node.js macrotasks. ## Errors and exit - An exception that no frame catches (thrown by a timer, a microtask, a Node-API finalizer or callback) goes to `process.on('uncaughtException')` listeners; without listeners the error is printed and the process exits with code **1**. - An unhandled promise rejection goes to `process.on('unhandledRejection')`; without listeners it is treated as an uncaught exception (Node.js default `--unhandled-rejections=throw`). - At the normal end of the script, `beforeExit` and `exit` are emitted and the host is **destroyed**: cleanup hooks, then finalizers ([architecture.md](architecture.md#teardown)). The exit code is `process.exitCode` (0 by default). - `process.exit(code)` and fatal exceptions end the process **immediately**, like Node.js: `exit` is emitted, the thread pool is shut down, and no cleanup hook or finalizer runs, nor is in-flight work waited for. - `napi_fatal_error` prints `FATAL ERROR: ` and aborts (`_exit(134)` on Windows). - On Windows, stdout and stderr are in binary mode: `\n` is written as is, as Node.js does, so a parent reading the pipe sees the same bytes on every platform. ## Not supported - ES modules (`import`, `.mjs`), `package.json` `"exports"` maps and conditional exports; - `worker_threads`, `async_hooks` (and therefore `AsyncLocalStorage`), `domain`; - most of the Node.js standard library (`fs`, `net`, `http`, `crypto`, ...): only the modules listed above exist.

docs.title: Testing
docs.markdown:
# Testing

quickjs-napi is tested against the behaviour of Node.js itself: most tests
are Node.js's own Node-API tests and the node-addon-api test suite, and our
own JavaScript tests also run under Node.js as a reference. CTest runs about
170 tests per configuration.

```sh
ctest --preset unix-debug                   # everything
ctest --preset unix-debug -R '^naa/'        # the node-addon-api suite
ctest --test-dir build/unix-debug -R js_host --output-on-failure
```

- [Test suites](#test-suites)
- [Consistency checks](#consistency-checks)
- [Sanitizers and leak checks](#sanitizers-and-leak-checks)
- [Tools](#tools)
- [Workflows](#workflows)

## Test suites

| Suite | CTest names | Source | What it covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Our JS tests | `js_hello`, `js_values`, `js_binary`, `js_node_api`, `js_host` | `test/js`, addons in `test/addons` | values, binary data, `node_api.h`, the executable's host features (child processes, `-e`, `-r`, `NODE_OPTIONS`) |
| Node.js parity | `node_parity_*` | the same `test/js` scripts | runs those tests under Node.js 22 with the same addon binaries: the expectations are checked against the reference implementation |
| Node.js conformance | `node/js-native-api/...`, `node/node-api/...` | `test/node` (Node.js v22.23.4) | 30 tests of `js-native-api` and 19 of `node-api`; see [test/node/README.md](../test/node/README.md) |
| node-addon-api | `naa/<module>` | `test/node-addon-api` (8.9.2) | 78 of the 83 test modules, each in the four binding variants (C++ exceptions, no exceptions, `Maybe`, custom namespace); see [the harness README](../test/node-addon-api/harness/README.md) |
| Embedding | `unit_embed` | `test/unit/test_embed.c` | what a JS test cannot observe: teardown order, handle-scope misuse, the error state, the finalizer queue of the embedding API |
| Fatal errors | `node/node-api/test_fatal/...` | `cmake/expect_abort.cmake` | runs a test that must abort (`napi_fatal_error`) and checks its output |

The test addons are built **exactly like node-gyp addons**: they do not link
against the library and resolve `napi_*` from the executable. The same
binaries load in Node.js, which is what makes the parity tests possible.

Tests not run, with the reason:

- node-addon-api modules that need `worker_threads`, `npm`, or test the npm
  package itself (5 of 83);
- Node.js tests that need `async_hooks` or `domain` (`test_async_context`,
  `test_make_callback_recurse`) or `worker_threads` (`test_worker_*`).

## Consistency checks

| Test | Checks |
|---|---|
| `stubs_up_to_date` | `src/stubs_generated.c` matches the set of functions implemented (`tools/gen_stubs.py --check`) |
| `exports_complete` | the executable exports every Node-API function (`tools/check_exports.py`) |

## Sanitizers and leak checks

- **Debug builds** use a Debug QuickJS, whose `JS_FreeRuntime` asserts that
  every object was released. Any `JSValue` leaked by the library aborts the
  test. This is why the library frees, at teardown, what addons never deleted.
- **`unix-asan`** runs everything under AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehavior
  Sanitizer and LeakSanitizer, QuickJS included. `test/lsan.supp` suppresses
  the leaks that Node.js and node-addon-api tests make **by design** (each
  entry says why).
- **`unix-tsan`** runs everything under ThreadSanitizer, QuickJS and libuv
  included: async work and thread-safe functions are exercised from several
  threads. CI reduces ASLR entropy for it.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `tools/gen_stubs.py` | regenerates `src/stubs_generated.c`: a stub (returning `napi_generic_failure` with a descriptive last-error message) for every function of the headers that no `src/*.c` defines. `--check` only verifies. |
| `tools/check_exports.py <executable>` | verifies that the executable exports every Node-API function (`nm` or `objdump`) |
| `tools/napi_decls.py` | parses the declarations of `js_native_api.h` and `node_api.h`; shared by the two tools above so that they agree on the function set |
| `tools/sync_node_tests.py <node-checkout>` | vendors Node.js's `test/js-native-api` and `test/node-api` tests into `test/node`, applies the declared patches and generates `tests.cmake` from each `binding.gyp` (the build needs neither Python nor node-gyp) |
| `tools/sync_node_addon_api.py <node-addon-api checkout>` | vendors the node-addon-api headers and test suite into `test/node-addon-api`, applies the declared patches and generates `tests.cmake` |

The vendored test directories are **generated**: do not edit them by hand.
Every change goes through the sync scripts, whose `PATCHES` / `SKIP_*` tables
give the reason for each difference from upstream.

## Workflows

### Implementing or changing a Node-API function

1. Implement it in the `src/` file of its area, following the Node.js source
   (`src/js_native_api_v8.cc`, `src/node_api.cc`) for statuses and edge
   cases. Use the macros of `qjsnapi_internal.h` (`NAPI_PREAMBLE`,
   `CHECK_ARG`, `CHECK_JS`, ...) so the error behaviour matches.
2. Run `python3 tools/gen_stubs.py` to drop its stub; `stubs_up_to_date` fails
   otherwise.
3. Enable the matching Node.js test in `tools/sync_node_tests.py` (`TESTS`) and
   re-run it, or add a case to a `test/js` script and its addon.
4. Run the suite in Debug (leak assertion) and under `unix-asan`.
5. Update the reference page in [doc/node-api](node-api/README.md) and, for a
   deviation, [compatibility.md](compatibility.md).

### Adding a JS test

Write it so that it runs **unchanged under both runtimes** (see
`test/js/test_hello.js`): it receives the addon directory as an argument and
throws on the first failed expectation. Register it in `CMakeLists.txt`
next to the other `js_*` tests; the `node_parity_*` variant is added the same
way.

### Updating the vendored suites

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch v22.23.4 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/nodejs/node
git -C node sparse-checkout set --no-cone /test/js-native-api/ /test/node-api/ /test/common/gc.js /test/common/tick.js /LICENSE
python3 tools/sync_node_tests.py node

python3 tools/sync_node_addon_api.py <node-addon-api checkout>
```

docs.title: Async work, thread-safe functions and the event loop
docs.markdown:
# Async work, thread-safe functions and the event loop

[Node-API reference](README.md) › Asynchronous APIs

Implemented in `src/async.c`, `src/tsfn.c` and `src/loop.c`, on libuv 1.51.
How these objects sit on the loop, and how teardown waits for them, is
described in [architecture.md](../architecture.md#the-event-loop).

| Group | Functions |
|---|---|
| Async work | [`napi_create_async_work`](#napi_create_async_work), [`napi_queue_async_work`](#napi_queue_async_work), [`napi_cancel_async_work`](#napi_cancel_async_work), [`napi_delete_async_work`](#napi_delete_async_work) |
| Thread-safe functions | [`napi_create_threadsafe_function`](#napi_create_threadsafe_function), [`napi_call_threadsafe_function`](#napi_call_threadsafe_function), [`napi_acquire_threadsafe_function`](#napi_acquire_threadsafe_function), [`napi_release_threadsafe_function`](#napi_release_threadsafe_function), [`napi_get_threadsafe_function_context`](#napi_get_threadsafe_function_context), [`napi_ref_threadsafe_function`](#napi_ref_threadsafe_function), [`napi_unref_threadsafe_function`](#napi_unref_threadsafe_function) |
| Event loop | [`napi_get_uv_event_loop`](#napi_get_uv_event_loop) |

## Threads

| Code | Runs on |
|---|---|
| `execute` of async work | a libuv thread-pool thread (`UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE` threads, 4 by default). Must not call Node-API functions that take an env. |
| `complete` of async work | the loop thread |
| `napi_call_threadsafe_function`, `napi_acquire_threadsafe_function`, `napi_release_threadsafe_function`, `napi_get_threadsafe_function_context` | any thread |
| `call_js_cb`, `thread_finalize_cb` of a thread-safe function | the loop thread |
| everything else | the loop thread |

Every callback the loop thread runs (`complete`, `call_js_cb`,
`thread_finalize_cb`) gets a handle scope and a callback scope; on return,
a pending exception is reported as uncaught and the checkpoint runs
(microtasks, `process.nextTick` in the executable).

---

## Async work

Runs a C function on the thread pool, then a completion on the loop thread.

```c
typedef struct { napi_async_work work; napi_deferred deferred; double input, output; } job;

static void Execute(napi_env env, void *data) {     /* thread pool */
  job *j = data;
  j->output = expensive(j->input);                  /* no Node-API here */
}

static void Complete(napi_env env, napi_status status, void *data) { /* loop */
  job *j = data;
  napi_value v;
  if (status == napi_ok) {
    napi_create_double(env, j->output, &v);
    napi_resolve_deferred(env, j->deferred, v);
  } else {                                           /* napi_cancelled */
    napi_get_undefined(env, &v);
    napi_reject_deferred(env, j->deferred, v);
  }
  napi_delete_async_work(env, j->work);
  free(j);
}

static napi_value Compute(napi_env env, napi_callback_info info) {
  job *j = calloc(1, sizeof *j);
  napi_value name, promise;
  /* ... read the input into j->input ... */
  napi_create_string_utf8(env, "compute", NAPI_AUTO_LENGTH, &name);
  napi_create_promise(env, &j->deferred, &promise);
  napi_create_async_work(env, NULL, name, Execute, Complete, j, &j->work);
  napi_queue_async_work(env, j->work);
  return promise;
}
```

### `napi_create_async_work`

```c
napi_status napi_create_async_work(napi_env env, napi_value async_resource,
                                   napi_value async_resource_name,
                                   napi_async_execute_callback execute,
                                   napi_async_complete_callback complete,
                                   void *data, napi_async_work *result);
```

Creates a work item; nothing runs until it is queued. `execute` is required,
`complete` is optional. `async_resource` (optional; `null`/`undefined` give
`napi_object_expected`) and `async_resource_name` (required; a symbol gives
`napi_string_expected`) are only validated: there is no `async_hooks`.

The item belongs to the addon until `napi_delete_async_work`. Items never
deleted are freed at teardown.

### `napi_queue_async_work`

```c
napi_status napi_queue_async_work(node_api_basic_env env,
                                  napi_async_work work);
```

Queues the item (`uv_queue_work`): `execute(env, data)` runs on a pool thread,
then `complete(env, status, data)` on the loop thread with `napi_ok`. The
queued item keeps the loop alive.

- Queuing an item that is already queued, or queuing while the host is being
  destroyed, returns `napi_generic_failure`.
- The item can be queued again once `complete` has started, including from
  `complete` itself.

### `napi_cancel_async_work`

```c
napi_status napi_cancel_async_work(node_api_basic_env env,
                                   napi_async_work work);
```

Cancels a queued item whose `execute` has not started (`uv_cancel`).
`complete` then still runs, with status `napi_cancelled`. When `execute` is
already running or done, cancellation fails with `napi_generic_failure`.

### `napi_delete_async_work`

```c
napi_status napi_delete_async_work(napi_env env, napi_async_work work);
```

Frees the item. Usually called from `complete`. Deleting an item that is
still queued is undefined behaviour in Node.js; here the item is only marked,
and freed after its `complete` has run.

At teardown, queued items are cancelled, in-flight ones are waited for, and
their `complete` runs with JavaScript disabled, so the addon can still free
its data.

## Thread-safe functions

A thread-safe function lets any thread schedule a call to JavaScript on the
loop thread. It is a port of Node 22's implementation: a queue protected by a
mutex, a `uv_async_t` to wake the loop thread, and up to 1000 calls dispatched
per wake-up. Its life cycle is shown in
[architecture.md](../architecture.md#thread-safe-functions).

```c
static void CallJs(napi_env env, napi_value js_cb, void *context, void *data) {
  int *value = data;
  if (env != NULL) {             /* NULL when the function is being finalized */
    napi_value undefined, arg;
    napi_get_undefined(env, &undefined);
    napi_create_int32(env, *value, &arg);
    napi_call_function(env, undefined, js_cb, 1, &arg, NULL);
  }
  free(value);
}

/* loop thread */
napi_create_threadsafe_function(env, js_callback, NULL, name, 0 /* unbounded */,
                                1 /* this thread */, NULL, NULL, NULL, CallJs,
                                &tsfn);
/* worker thread */
int *v = malloc(sizeof *v); *v = 42;
napi_call_threadsafe_function(tsfn, v, napi_tsfn_blocking);
napi_release_threadsafe_function(tsfn, napi_tsfn_release);
```

### `napi_create_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_create_threadsafe_function(
    napi_env env, napi_value func, napi_value async_resource,
    napi_value async_resource_name, size_t max_queue_size,
    size_t initial_thread_count, void *thread_finalize_data,
    napi_finalize thread_finalize_cb, void *context,
    napi_threadsafe_function_call_js call_js_cb,
    napi_threadsafe_function *result);
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `func` | JavaScript function passed to `call_js_cb` (kept with a strong reference); optional when `call_js_cb` is given, otherwise it must be a function (`napi_invalid_arg`) |
| `async_resource`, `async_resource_name` | validated only (no `async_hooks`); the name is required |
| `max_queue_size` | 0 for an unbounded queue; otherwise producers block (or get `napi_queue_full`) when it is full |
| `initial_thread_count` | number of threads using the function, at least 1 (`napi_invalid_arg` otherwise) |
| `thread_finalize_data`, `thread_finalize_cb` | `thread_finalize_cb(env, thread_finalize_data, context)` runs on the loop thread when the function is finalized |
| `context` | any pointer, passed to `call_js_cb` and `thread_finalize_cb` |
| `call_js_cb` | `call_js_cb(env, func, context, data)` for each queued item; without it, `func` is called with no arguments and `this = undefined` |

The function starts **referenced**: it keeps the loop alive until it is
finalized or unreferenced. It registers an internal cleanup hook, so it is
closed at teardown.

### `napi_call_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_call_threadsafe_function(
    napi_threadsafe_function func, void *data,
    napi_threadsafe_function_call_mode is_blocking);
```

Queues `data` for a call of `call_js_cb` on the loop thread. Callable from any
thread.

| Result | When |
|---|---|
| `napi_ok` | queued |
| `napi_queue_full` | bounded queue full and `napi_tsfn_nonblocking` |
| (blocks) | bounded queue full and `napi_tsfn_blocking`: waits for room. Do not do this on the loop thread: it would deadlock (`napi_would_deadlock` is not returned, as in Node.js 22) |
| `napi_closing` | the function is closing (aborted, or finalized at teardown); this call also releases the caller's thread count, so the caller must not call `napi_release_threadsafe_function` afterwards |
| `napi_invalid_arg` | `func` is `NULL`, or it is closing and no thread holds it any more |

### `napi_acquire_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_acquire_threadsafe_function(napi_threadsafe_function func);
```

Increments the thread count, before handing the function to another thread.
`napi_closing` if it is already closing.

### `napi_release_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_release_threadsafe_function(
    napi_threadsafe_function func,
    napi_threadsafe_function_release_mode mode);
```

Decrements the thread count. When it reaches 0 the function closes once its
queue is drained. With `napi_tsfn_abort` it closes **now**: blocked producers
wake up, further calls get `napi_closing`, and items still queued are handed
to `call_js_cb` with `env == NULL` (and `func == NULL`) so that their data can
be freed. `napi_invalid_arg` when the count is already 0.

### `napi_get_threadsafe_function_context`

```c
napi_status napi_get_threadsafe_function_context(napi_threadsafe_function func,
                                                 void **result);
```

Stores the `context` given at creation. Callable from any thread.
`napi_invalid_arg` for `NULL` arguments (Node.js aborts).

### `napi_ref_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_ref_threadsafe_function(node_api_basic_env env,
                                         napi_threadsafe_function func);
```

Makes the function keep the loop alive again (`uv_ref` on its async handle).
Loop thread only.

### `napi_unref_threadsafe_function`

```c
napi_status napi_unref_threadsafe_function(node_api_basic_env env,
                                           napi_threadsafe_function func);
```

Lets the loop exit while the function is still open (`uv_unref`): useful for a
background producer that should not keep the process running. Loop thread
only.

### Exceptions in `call_js_cb`

An exception left pending by `call_js_cb` (or `thread_finalize_cb`) has no
JavaScript caller. For modules built for **Node-API ≥ 10** it is reported as
uncaught (`process.on('uncaughtException')`). For older modules it is
dropped with a one-time `DEP0168` deprecation warning on stderr, as in
Node.js, unless the host forces the policy
(`--force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy`, or
[`qjsnapi_host_set_force_uncaught_exceptions_policy`](../embedding.md#qjsnapi_host_set_force_uncaught_exceptions_policy)).

Exceptions from async work `complete` callbacks and from finalizers are always
reported as uncaught.

## Event loop

### `napi_get_uv_event_loop`

```c
napi_status napi_get_uv_event_loop(node_api_basic_env env,
                                   struct uv_loop_s **loop);
```

Stores the libuv loop of the host: the one the embedder runs and the
executable runs until nothing referenced is left. Addons may add their own
handles to it (timers, sockets, `uv_async_t`); they must close them before
teardown ends, typically from an
[async cleanup hook](environment.md#napi_add_async_cleanup_hook). The
executable exports every `uv_*` function, so addons built with node-gyp's
`uv.h` link against it like against `node`.

docs.title: ArrayBuffer, TypedArray, DataView, BigInt, Date, Promise
docs.markdown:
# ArrayBuffer, TypedArray, DataView, BigInt, Date, Promise [Node-API reference](README.md) › Binary data and builtins Implemented in `src/builtins.c`. Semantics follow Node.js 22.23 / V8 and are checked against Node.js by `test/js/test_binary.js`. | Group | Functions | |---|---| | ArrayBuffer | [`napi_create_arraybuffer`](#napi_create_arraybuffer), [`napi_create_external_arraybuffer`](#napi_create_external_arraybuffer), [`napi_is_arraybuffer`](#napi_is_arraybuffer), [`napi_get_arraybuffer_info`](#napi_get_arraybuffer_info), [`napi_detach_arraybuffer`](#napi_detach_arraybuffer), [`napi_is_detached_arraybuffer`](#napi_is_detached_arraybuffer) | | TypedArray | [`napi_create_typedarray`](#napi_create_typedarray), [`napi_is_typedarray`](#napi_is_typedarray), [`napi_get_typedarray_info`](#napi_get_typedarray_info) | | DataView | [`napi_create_dataview`](#napi_create_dataview), [`napi_is_dataview`](#napi_is_dataview), [`napi_get_dataview_info`](#napi_get_dataview_info) | | BigInt | [`napi_create_bigint_int64`](#napi_create_bigint_int64), [`napi_create_bigint_uint64`](#napi_create_bigint_uint64), [`napi_create_bigint_words`](#napi_create_bigint_words), [`napi_get_value_bigint_int64`](#napi_get_value_bigint_int64), [`napi_get_value_bigint_uint64`](#napi_get_value_bigint_uint64), [`napi_get_value_bigint_words`](#napi_get_value_bigint_words) | | Date | [`napi_create_date`](#napi_create_date), [`napi_is_date`](#napi_is_date), [`napi_get_date_value`](#napi_get_date_value) | | Promise | [`napi_create_promise`](#napi_create_promise), [`napi_resolve_deferred`](#napi_resolve_deferred), [`napi_reject_deferred`](#napi_reject_deferred), [`napi_is_promise`](#napi_is_promise) | ## Implementation notes - **Type checks use class IDs.** QuickJS does not export its class ID enum, so the IDs of `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `DataView`, `Date` and the typed arrays are found at startup by probing one instance of each. A check such as `napi_is_date` is therefore exact: an object whose prototype is `Date.prototype` is not a Date, and a Date from another realm is one. - **Accessors are captured.** The `DataView` and `%TypedArray%` getters, `Date.prototype.getTime` and the `ArrayBuffer` / `DataView` constructors are captured before any user code runs: patching the globals has no effect. - **Pointers into buffers stay valid while the buffer is alive and not detached.** QuickJS never moves ArrayBuffer memory, but resizing a resizable ArrayBuffer may reallocate it: read `data` again after JavaScript ran. ```mermaid flowchart LR AB["ArrayBuffer
(or SharedArrayBuffer)"] --> TA["TypedArray
type, byte_offset, length"] AB --> DV["DataView
byte_offset, byte_length"] AB --> BUF["Buffer
(Uint8Array subclass,
see node-specific.md)"] TA -. "data = buffer data + byte_offset" .-> AB ``` --- ## ArrayBuffer ### `napi_create_arraybuffer` ```c napi_status napi_create_arraybuffer(napi_env env, size_t byte_length, void **data, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a **zero-filled** ArrayBuffer of `byte_length` bytes (through the `ArrayBuffer` constructor, so QuickJS's size limits apply: too large a size throws a `RangeError`, `napi_pending_exception`). `data` (optional) receives a pointer to the contents, `NULL` for a zero-length buffer. ### `napi_create_external_arraybuffer` ```c napi_status napi_create_external_arraybuffer( napi_env env, void *external_data, size_t byte_length, node_api_basic_finalize finalize_cb, void *finalize_hint, napi_value *result); ``` Creates an ArrayBuffer over memory owned by the addon. The memory is **used in place**, never copied nor freed by QuickJS. When the ArrayBuffer is collected, `finalize_cb(env, external_data, finalize_hint)` runs (queued, from the event loop, as in Node.js), and the addon frees the memory there. `external_data == NULL` creates a buffer that reads as **detached** (V8 has no backing store for `NULL` data). ### `napi_is_arraybuffer` ```c napi_status napi_is_arraybuffer(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *result); ``` `true` for an `ArrayBuffer` (detached ones included). `false` for a `SharedArrayBuffer`, as in V8. ### `napi_get_arraybuffer_info` ```c napi_status napi_get_arraybuffer_info(napi_env env, napi_value arraybuffer, void **data, size_t *byte_length); ``` Stores the contents pointer and size; both outputs are optional. Accepts an `ArrayBuffer` or, like Node.js 22.23, a `SharedArrayBuffer` (`napi_invalid_arg` for anything else). An empty or detached buffer has `data == NULL` and length 0. For a resizable buffer the current length is reported. ### `napi_detach_arraybuffer` ```c napi_status napi_detach_arraybuffer(napi_env env, napi_value arraybuffer); ``` Detaches an ArrayBuffer, as `structuredClone(ab, {transfer: [ab]})` would: its length becomes 0 and every view on it reads as empty. `napi_arraybuffer_expected` for anything other than an `ArrayBuffer` (every non-shared QuickJS ArrayBuffer is detachable). Detaching an external buffer does not run its finalizer early; the finalizer still runs when the object is collected. ### `napi_is_detached_arraybuffer` ```c napi_status napi_is_detached_arraybuffer(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *result); ``` `true` when `value` is an `ArrayBuffer` that has been detached, like V8's `WasDetached()`; `false` for any other value. ## TypedArray Supported types (`napi_typedarray_type`): `napi_int8_array`, `napi_uint8_array`, `napi_uint8_clamped_array`, `napi_int16_array`, `napi_uint16_array`, `napi_int32_array`, `napi_uint32_array`, `napi_float32_array`, `napi_float64_array`, `napi_bigint64_array`, `napi_biguint64_array` and `napi_float16_array`. `napi_float16_array` is supported because QuickJS has `Float16Array`; Node.js 22 returns `napi_invalid_arg` for it. ### `napi_create_typedarray` ```c napi_status napi_create_typedarray(napi_env env, napi_typedarray_type type, size_t length, napi_value arraybuffer, size_t byte_offset, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a typed array of `length` elements over `arraybuffer` (an `ArrayBuffer` or a `SharedArrayBuffer`), starting at `byte_offset`. Errors are the same `RangeError`s as in Node.js, thrown with the function returning `napi_generic_failure` and the exception pending: | Condition | Code | Message | |---|---|---| | `byte_offset` not a multiple of the element size | `ERR_NAPI_INVALID_TYPEDARRAY_ALIGNMENT` | `start offset of Int32Array should be a multiple of 4` | | `byte_offset + length * size` beyond the buffer | `ERR_NAPI_INVALID_TYPEDARRAY_LENGTH` | `Invalid typed array length` | An unknown `type` or a non-buffer `arraybuffer` gives `napi_invalid_arg`. ### `napi_is_typedarray` ```c napi_status napi_is_typedarray(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *result); ``` `true` for an instance of any of the 12 typed array types, Buffers included. `false` for a DataView. ### `napi_get_typedarray_info` ```c napi_status napi_get_typedarray_info(napi_env env, napi_value typedarray, napi_typedarray_type *type, size_t *length, void **data, napi_value *arraybuffer, size_t *byte_offset); ``` Stores, for every non-`NULL` output: the element type, the length **in elements**, a pointer to the first element (buffer data + offset), the underlying ArrayBuffer and the byte offset. `napi_invalid_arg` when `typedarray` is not a typed array. - A view whose buffer is detached, or that is out of bounds after its resizable buffer shrank, reports length 0. - A length-tracking view (created without a length on a resizable buffer) reports its current length. - For an out-of-bounds, non-detached view the byte offset is reported as 0; V8 reports the stored offset, which QuickJS does not expose. ## DataView ### `napi_create_dataview` ```c napi_status napi_create_dataview(napi_env env, size_t length, napi_value arraybuffer, size_t byte_offset, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a DataView of `length` bytes over an `ArrayBuffer`, starting at `byte_offset` (`napi_invalid_arg` for anything other than an ArrayBuffer). When the range exceeds the buffer, throws a `RangeError` with code `ERR_NAPI_INVALID_DATAVIEW_ARGS` ("byte_offset + byte_length should be less than or equal to the size in bytes of the array passed in") and returns `napi_pending_exception`, as in Node.js. ### `napi_is_dataview` ```c napi_status napi_is_dataview(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *result); ``` `true` for a DataView. ### `napi_get_dataview_info` ```c napi_status napi_get_dataview_info(napi_env env, napi_value dataview, size_t *bytelength, void **data, napi_value *arraybuffer, size_t *byte_offset); ``` Stores, for every non-`NULL` output: the length in bytes, a pointer to the first byte, the underlying ArrayBuffer and the byte offset. On a detached buffer, length and offset are 0, as V8 reports. `napi_invalid_arg` when `dataview` is not a DataView. ## BigInt QuickJS limits a BigInt to **2^20 bits** (16384 64-bit words); V8 allows 2^30. ### `napi_create_bigint_int64` ```c napi_status napi_create_bigint_int64(napi_env env, int64_t value, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a BigInt from a signed 64-bit integer. ### `napi_create_bigint_uint64` ```c napi_status napi_create_bigint_uint64(napi_env env, uint64_t value, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a BigInt from an unsigned 64-bit integer. ### `napi_create_bigint_words` ```c napi_status napi_create_bigint_words(napi_env env, int sign_bit, size_t word_count, const uint64_t *words, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a BigInt from its magnitude as little-endian 64-bit words (`words[0]` is the least significant) and a sign (`sign_bit != 0` for negative). Zero words, or words that are all zero, give `0n` whatever the sign. - `word_count > INT_MAX`: `napi_invalid_arg`. - `word_count` above 16384: `RangeError: Maximum BigInt size exceeded`, with `napi_pending_exception`, checked before `words` is read (V8 throws the same error past its own limit). - The conversion goes through a hexadecimal string: O(n) in the number of words. ### `napi_get_value_bigint_int64` ```c napi_status napi_get_value_bigint_int64(napi_env env, napi_value value, int64_t *result, bool *lossless); ``` Stores the BigInt modulo 2^64 as a signed integer (two's complement), and `*lossless = true` when that is exactly the value. Both outputs are required. `napi_bigint_expected` when `value` is not a BigInt. ### `napi_get_value_bigint_uint64` ```c napi_status napi_get_value_bigint_uint64(napi_env env, napi_value value, uint64_t *result, bool *lossless); ``` Same, as an unsigned integer (`-1n` gives `UINT64_MAX`, not lossless). ### `napi_get_value_bigint_words` ```c napi_status napi_get_value_bigint_words(napi_env env, napi_value value, int *sign_bit, size_t *word_count, uint64_t *words); ``` Reads a BigInt as sign and magnitude words, like V8's `BigInt::ToWordsArray`: - **Count only:** with `sign_bit` and `words` both `NULL`, stores in `*word_count` the number of words the value needs. - **Read:** `*word_count` is the capacity of `words` on input. The low words that fit are written; on output `*word_count` is the number of words the value needs (which may be more than were written). `*sign_bit` is 1 for a negative value. - `0n` has no words and sign 0. ```c size_t n; napi_get_value_bigint_words(env, value, NULL, &n, NULL); uint64_t *w = malloc(n * sizeof *w); int sign; napi_get_value_bigint_words(env, value, &sign, &n, w); ``` ## Date ### `napi_create_date` ```c napi_status napi_create_date(napi_env env, double time, napi_value *result); ``` Creates a Date from milliseconds since the epoch. `TimeClip` applies: values beyond ±8.64e15 or non-finite give an invalid date (`NaN` time), as in V8. ### `napi_is_date` ```c napi_status napi_is_date(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *is_date); ``` `true` for a Date object. ### `napi_get_date_value` ```c napi_status napi_get_date_value(napi_env env, napi_value value, double *result); ``` Stores the time value in milliseconds (`NaN` for an invalid date), using the `Date.prototype.getTime` captured at startup. `napi_date_expected` when `value` is not a Date. ## Promise A `napi_deferred` is the pair of resolving functions of a new promise. It is **released by the first resolve or reject**; deferreds never concluded are freed at teardown. ```c napi_deferred deferred; napi_value promise; napi_create_promise(env, &deferred, &promise); /* return `promise` to JavaScript; later, e.g. in an async work complete: */ napi_resolve_deferred(env, deferred, value); ``` ### `napi_create_promise` ```c napi_status napi_create_promise(napi_env env, napi_deferred *deferred, napi_value *promise); ``` Creates a pending promise and its deferred. Both outputs are required. ### `napi_resolve_deferred` ```c napi_status napi_resolve_deferred(napi_env env, napi_deferred deferred, napi_value resolution); ``` Resolves the promise with `resolution` (a thenable is followed, as with the `resolve` function of `new Promise`) and frees the deferred. Reactions run at the next microtask checkpoint, not synchronously. ### `napi_reject_deferred` ```c napi_status napi_reject_deferred(napi_env env, napi_deferred deferred, napi_value rejection); ``` Rejects the promise with `rejection` and frees the deferred. A rejection nobody handles is reported by the host as an unhandled rejection. ### `napi_is_promise` ```c napi_status napi_is_promise(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *is_promise); ``` `true` for a native Promise object (not for other thenables).

# Environment, versions and cleanup hooks

[Node-API reference](README.md) › Environment

Implemented in `src/env.c` and `src/loader.c`.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`napi_get_last_error_info`](#napi_get_last_error_info) | details of the last failed call |
| [`napi_get_version`](#napi_get_version) | highest supported Node-API version |
| [`napi_get_node_version`](#napi_get_node_version) | the Node.js version that is emulated |
| [`node_api_get_module_file_name`](#node_api_get_module_file_name) | URL of the addon file |
| [`napi_add_env_cleanup_hook`](#napi_add_env_cleanup_hook) | run a function at teardown |
| [`napi_remove_env_cleanup_hook`](#napi_remove_env_cleanup_hook) | unregister it |
| [`napi_add_async_cleanup_hook`](#napi_add_async_cleanup_hook) | asynchronous teardown step |
| [`napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook`](#napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook) | unregister it, or signal it is done |
| [`napi_fatal_error`](#napi_fatal_error) | abort the process |
| [`napi_module_register`](#napi_module_register) | legacy module registration |

---

### `napi_get_last_error_info`

```c
napi_status napi_get_last_error_info(node_api_basic_env env,
                                     const napi_extended_error_info **result);
```

Returns a pointer to the env's last-error record: `error_code` is the status of
the last Node-API call that failed (or `napi_ok`), `error_message` a static
English message (see the [status table](README.md#status-codes-and-the-last-error)).
`engine_error_code` and `engine_reserved` are always `0` / `NULL`.

- The record belongs to the env and is overwritten by the next call: copy what
  you need before calling another function.
- This function never changes the last error itself, so it can be called
  repeatedly. It always returns `napi_ok` (or `napi_invalid_arg` for a `NULL`
  argument).
- Each native callback starts with a clear last error, as in Node.js.

### `napi_get_version`

```c
napi_status napi_get_version(node_api_basic_env env, uint32_t *result);
```

Stores `10`, the highest Node-API version this build supports (the same value
as `qjsnapi_napi_version()`). Experimental APIs (`NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL`) are not
provided.

### `napi_get_node_version`

```c
napi_status napi_get_node_version(node_api_basic_env env,
                                  const napi_node_version **version);
```

Stores a pointer to a static record `{ major: 22, minor: 23, patch: 4,
release: "quickjs-napi" }`: the Node.js release whose Node-API behaviour is
reproduced. Addons that check for a minimum Node.js version therefore see
22.23.4. The executable's `process.version` reports the same.

### `node_api_get_module_file_name`

```c
napi_status node_api_get_module_file_name(node_api_basic_env env,
                                          const char **result);
```

Stores the absolute `file://` URL of the addon this env belongs to, encoded
like Node's `url.pathToFileURL` (percent-encoding, Windows drive letters as
`file:///C:/...`). The string lives as long as the env. For a static addon
(`qjsnapi_init_static_addon`) it is the name given by the embedder.

### `napi_add_env_cleanup_hook`

```c
napi_status napi_add_env_cleanup_hook(node_api_basic_env env,
                                      napi_cleanup_hook fun, void *arg);
```

Registers `fun(arg)` to run when the env is torn down
(`qjsnapi_host_destroy`, or the normal end of the executable). Hooks run in
**reverse order of registration** (LIFO), interleaved with the async cleanup
hooks and the library's own hooks (thread-safe functions), with JavaScript
already disabled.

- Registering the same `(fun, arg)` pair twice is a **fatal error**, as in
  Node.js (where it is a `CHECK` failure).
- Hooks do **not** run when the executable ends with `process.exit()` or a
  fatal exception, as in Node.js.

### `napi_remove_env_cleanup_hook`

```c
napi_status napi_remove_env_cleanup_hook(node_api_basic_env env,
                                         napi_cleanup_hook fun, void *arg);
```

Unregisters the hook registered with the same `(fun, arg)`. Removing a pair
that is not registered does nothing and returns `napi_ok`.

### `napi_add_async_cleanup_hook`

```c
napi_status napi_add_async_cleanup_hook(
    node_api_basic_env env, napi_async_cleanup_hook hook, void *arg,
    napi_async_cleanup_hook_handle *remove_handle);
```

Registers a cleanup step that may take time, such as closing a libuv handle.
At teardown `hook(handle, arg)` is called in LIFO order with the other hooks;
the teardown then **keeps running the event loop** until the addon calls
`napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook(handle)`, typically from a `uv_close`
callback.

`remove_handle` may be `NULL` when the hook is never removed early; the hook
then receives the handle as its first argument.

```c
static void on_close(uv_handle_t *h) {
  napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook(((my_state *)h->data)->cleanup_handle);
}
static void cleanup(napi_async_cleanup_hook_handle handle, void *arg) {
  my_state *s = arg;
  s->cleanup_handle = handle;
  uv_close((uv_handle_t *)&s->timer, on_close);
}
/* in init: */
napi_add_async_cleanup_hook(env, cleanup, state, NULL);
```

### `napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook`

```c
napi_status napi_remove_async_cleanup_hook(
    napi_async_cleanup_hook_handle remove_handle);
```

Has two meanings, as in Node.js:

- **before teardown**, it unregisters the hook, which will not run;
- **after the hook started**, it signals that the asynchronous cleanup is
  complete, so the teardown can stop waiting for it.

The handle is freed in both cases and must not be used again. Returns
`napi_invalid_arg` for `NULL`.

### `napi_fatal_error`

```c
NAPI_NO_RETURN void napi_fatal_error(const char *location, size_t location_len,
                                     const char *message, size_t message_len);
```

Prints `FATAL ERROR: <location> <message>` on stderr and ends the process
immediately: `abort()` on Linux and macOS, `_exit(134)` on Windows (like
Node.js, which avoids the Windows Error Reporting dialog). No cleanup runs.
Both lengths accept `NAPI_AUTO_LENGTH`; `location` and `message` may be
`NULL`.

### `napi_module_register`

```c
void napi_module_register(napi_module *mod);
```

Legacy registration used by addons built with the old `NAPI_MODULE` macro
from a static constructor. When called **while `qjsnapi_load_addon` is opening
a library**, the module is attached to that load and its `nm_register_func`
becomes the initializer (only when the library does not export
`napi_register_module_v1`, which takes precedence). The record is remembered,
so loading the same file again reuses it even though the constructor does not
run a second time.

Called outside of a load (for instance by an addon linked into the
executable), it prints a warning and does nothing: use
[`qjsnapi_init_static_addon`](../embedding.md#qjsnapi_init_static_addon)
instead. A legacy module with no `nm_register_func` fails to load with
`Module has no declared entry point.`

# Errors and exceptions

[Node-API reference](README.md) › Errors

Implemented in `src/error.c`. The model (status codes plus a pending
JavaScript exception) is described in
[architecture.md](../architecture.md#errors-and-exceptions).

| Group | Functions |
|---|---|
| Create an error object | [`napi_create_error`](#napi_create_error), [`napi_create_type_error`](#napi_create_type_error), [`napi_create_range_error`](#napi_create_range_error), [`node_api_create_syntax_error`](#node_api_create_syntax_error) |
| Throw | [`napi_throw`](#napi_throw), [`napi_throw_error`](#napi_throw_error), [`napi_throw_type_error`](#napi_throw_type_error), [`napi_throw_range_error`](#napi_throw_range_error), [`node_api_throw_syntax_error`](#node_api_throw_syntax_error) |
| Inspect | [`napi_is_error`](#napi_is_error), [`napi_is_exception_pending`](#napi_is_exception_pending), [`napi_get_and_clear_last_exception`](#napi_get_and_clear_last_exception) |

## Pending exceptions

QuickJS keeps at most **one pending exception** on the runtime, and
quickjs-napi uses it directly:

- a failed call into JavaScript leaves the exception pending and returns
  `napi_pending_exception`;
- `napi_throw*` make an exception pending and return `napi_ok`;
- while an exception is pending, [functions that run JavaScript](README.md#functions-that-run-javascript)
  refuse to start, but value creation and the functions on this page still
  work;
- when the native callback returns, a pending exception propagates to the
  JavaScript caller. With no JavaScript caller (finalizers, async work,
  thread-safe functions) it is reported as uncaught.

A typical error path:

```c
napi_value result;
napi_status s = napi_call_function(env, recv, fn, 0, NULL, &result);
if (s == napi_pending_exception) {
  napi_value exc;
  napi_get_and_clear_last_exception(env, &exc); /* handle it here ... */
  /* ... or simply return NULL and let it propagate */
}
```

## Error objects

The four error constructors (`Error`, `TypeError`, `RangeError`,
`SyntaxError`) are captured when the host is created, so replacing
`globalThis.Error` later does not change what these functions create. Like
Node.js, they create `new Ctor(message)` and, when a code is given, set an
own enumerable `code` property after construction.

---

## Create an error object

These functions only create the object; nothing is thrown. They work while an
exception is pending.

### `napi_create_error`

```c
napi_status napi_create_error(napi_env env, napi_value code, napi_value msg,
                              napi_value *result);
```

Creates `new Error(msg)`. `msg` must be a string; `code` is optional (`NULL`)
or a string, set as `error.code`. Either one not being a string gives
`napi_string_expected`.

### `napi_create_type_error`

```c
napi_status napi_create_type_error(napi_env env, napi_value code,
                                   napi_value msg, napi_value *result);
```

Same with `TypeError`.

### `napi_create_range_error`

```c
napi_status napi_create_range_error(napi_env env, napi_value code,
                                    napi_value msg, napi_value *result);
```

Same with `RangeError`.

### `node_api_create_syntax_error`

```c
napi_status node_api_create_syntax_error(napi_env env, napi_value code,
                                         napi_value msg, napi_value *result);
```

Same with `SyntaxError`.

## Throw

### `napi_throw`

```c
napi_status napi_throw(napi_env env, napi_value error);
```

Throws `error`, which may be any value (not only an Error object). Returns
`napi_ok`; the exception is now pending.

### `napi_throw_error`

```c
napi_status napi_throw_error(napi_env env, const char *code, const char *msg);
```

Creates and throws `new Error(msg)` with an optional `code` (`NULL` for none).
`msg` is a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string and is required.

### `napi_throw_type_error`

```c
napi_status napi_throw_type_error(napi_env env, const char *code,
                                  const char *msg);
```

Same with `TypeError`.

### `napi_throw_range_error`

```c
napi_status napi_throw_range_error(napi_env env, const char *code,
                                   const char *msg);
```

Same with `RangeError`.

### `node_api_throw_syntax_error`

```c
napi_status node_api_throw_syntax_error(napi_env env, const char *code,
                                        const char *msg);
```

Same with `SyntaxError`.

All `napi_throw*` functions refuse to start (`napi_pending_exception`) when an
exception is already pending: an exception never silently replaces another.

## Inspect

### `napi_is_error`

```c
napi_status napi_is_error(napi_env env, napi_value value, bool *result);
```

`true` when `value` is an Error object: an object created by a builtin error
constructor or a subclass of one (QuickJS `JS_IsError`). An ordinary object
whose prototype chain contains `Error.prototype` is not an Error.

### `napi_is_exception_pending`

```c
napi_status napi_is_exception_pending(napi_env env, bool *result);
```

`true` when an exception is pending on the context.

### `napi_get_and_clear_last_exception`

```c
napi_status napi_get_and_clear_last_exception(napi_env env,
                                              napi_value *result);
```

Takes the pending exception: stores it in `result` and clears it, so
JavaScript can run again. When no exception is pending, stores `undefined`.
